papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with central nervous system (CNS) metastases poses significant treatment challenges, as first-generation EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) (FGET) show limited CNS efficacy. Although third-generation EGFR-TKIs (TGET) exhibit superior CNS penetration, the optimal choice for first-line treatment remains debated. This meta-analysis aims to resolve this controversy by directly comparing the CNS efficacy of TGET vs. FGET in patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC and CNS metastases. METHODS: A thorough literature search was performed for phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TGET and FGET in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and CNS metastases. The primary outcome was CNS-progression-free survival (PFS), and secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS), PFS, CNS response rates, and adverse events (AEs). The study was registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024629581). RESULTS: A total of 5 phase 3 RCTs (AENEAS, FLAURA, FURLONG, IBIO-103, and LASER301) met the inclusion criteria. TGET demonstrated superior efficacy in CNS-PFS [hazard ratio (HR): 0.44 (0.33, 0.58), P<0.001], PFS [HR: 0.44 (0.35, 0.54), P<0.001], CNS-objective response rate (ORR) [risk ratio (RR): 1.32 (1.15, 1.52), P<0.001], CNS-complete response (CR) [RR: 3.40 (1.39, 8.28), P=0.007], and CNS-duration of response (DOR) [HR: 0.39 (0.21, 0.73), P=0.003]. The CNS-PFS rate at 4-24 months and PFS at 10-24 months were significantly higher in the TGET group. OS data were available from only 2 of the 5 included phase 3 RCTs. In this analysis, OS numerically favored the TGET group but did not reach statistical significance [HR: 0.79 (0.55, 1.13), P=0.20]. At the cutoff time, more CNS progressions were found in the FGET [RR: 0.59 (0.44, 0.80), P=0.001]. Additionally, less grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) were found in the TGET group [RR: 0.67 (0.46, 0.98), P=0.04]. CONCLUSIONS: TGET appeared to be better than FGET for patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and CNS metastases, showing improved survival, CNS efficacy, and safety.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thoracoscopic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair, although minimally invasive, can cause substantial postoperative pain. Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) provides effective chest wall analgesia, and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), a long-acting local anesthetic with sustained release, may prolong analgesic duration. We investigated whether ultrasound-guided TPVB using long-acting LB improves postoperative analgesia without compromising cardiovascular safety compared with ropivacaine (RP). METHODS: This randomized, assessor-blinded trial enrolled 94 patients undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, who were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ultrasound-guided TPVB with either LB or RP. Eligibility criteria included age 18-55 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) II-III, New York Heart Association (NYHA) II-III, and ejection fraction (EF) >50%. Randomization was computer-generated with sealed envelopes. Safety monitoring included continuous electrocardiography (ECG) for arrhythmias, with Clavien-Dindo grading and Naranjo causality assessment. The primary endpoint was the numerical rating scale (NRS, 0-10) pain score during coughing at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included NRS scores at other time points, 72-h opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME), time to first rescue analgesia, extended analgesia outcomes [postoperative days 4-7 (POD4-POD7)], perioperative hemodynamics, postoperative recovery, cardiac/inflammatory biomarker trajectories, and adverse events (with postoperative arrhythmias analyzed separately). RESULTS: Baseline demographic, clinical, and intraoperative variables were well-balanced between groups (all P>0.05). Compared with RP, LB was associated with lower NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing from extubation through 72 h (all P<0.05), including the primary endpoint at 24 h. LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%). CONCLUSIONS: In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2500112278, retrospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on November 12, 2025.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thoracoscopic lung tumor surgery is associated with significant postoperative pain. While liposomal bupivacaine (LB) provides prolonged analgesia, its higher cost and extended duration profile have not been directly compared with ropivacaine, a commonly used long‑acting local anesthetic in paravertebral blockade. Whether these differences translate into meaningful clinical benefits remains uncertain. This study assessed the utility of LB as an alternative method for pain control through a comparison with ropivacaine. METHODS: In this prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 200 patients scheduled for elective thoracoscopic lung tumor surgery were randomly assigned to control [paravertebral block (PVB) with 10 mL of 0.75% ropivacaine; n=100] or experimental (PVB with 10 mL of 1.3% LB; n=100) groups. Postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) with hydromorphone (10 mg/180 mL; background: 0 mL/h; bolus: 5 mL; lockout: 15 min) was initiated in all patients. Primary outcomes included pain scores of the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) at rest and during movement at 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours post-operation; and the cumulative morphine milligram equivalent (MME) at 0-<24, 24-<48, 48-72, and 0-72 hours (including both PCIA and rescue analgesics). Secondary outcomes included PCIA doses, rescue analgesia, and adverse events within 72 hours. Exploratory 3‑month telephone follow‑up assessed pain presence during usual activities and breathing. RESULTS: Of 200 randomized patients, 184 completed in‑hospital follow‑up (92 per group) and were included in the primary analysis.Sixteen patients were excluded after randomization (3 due to cancelled surgery, 4 due to reoperation, 5 due to postoperative complications, and 4 due to withdrawal of consent). Compared with the control group, the LB group showed significantly lower resting NRS scores at 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours (P=0.04, 0.04, 0.02, and 0.01, respectively) and dynamic NRS scores at all time points (6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours) (P=0.02, 0.001, 0.002, 0.04, 0.03, and 0.046, respectively). MME consumption was significantly reduced in the LB group during the 48- to 72-hour interval (P=0.03) and cumulatively over 0-72 hours (P=0.03). The number of delivered PCIA doses was significantly lower in the LB group during the 48- to 72-hour interval (P=0.02), with no significant differences in the 0 to 24- or 24- to 48-hour intervals. Rescue analgesia rates (3.3% vs. 5.4%, P=0.72) and the incidence of any adverse events (42.4% vs. 51.1%, P=0.30) did not differ significantly between groups. At 3 months, 175 patients completed follow-up (control: 90; LB: 85); fewer LB patients reported pain (17.6% vs. 21.1%), though no statistical comparison was performed. CONCLUSIONS: In thoracoscopic lung tumor surgery, PVB with LB provides improved and sustained postoperative analgesia and reduces opioid consumption as compared with ropivacaine, without increasing the incidence of adverse events. It may represent a safe and effective single-injection alternative for multimodal analgesia. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400093464.

papers.abstract_en: Definitive chemoradiotherapy followed by immunotherapy consolidation is the current standard of care for limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC). We conducted a randomized phase II trial (ChiCTR2000032275) to evaluate a camrelizumab-based induction-consolidation strategy in previously untreated patients with LS-SCLC. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive induction camrelizumab plus etoposide-platinum followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and camrelizumab consolidation (camrelizumab group), or induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent CRT alone (cCRT group). The primary endpoint was the 1‑year progression‑free survival (PFS) rate. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. Between November 2020 and April 2024, 41 patients were enrolled. At a median follow‑up of 32.1 months (interquartile range [IQR]: 26.4-38.7), ORR was 100% in the camrelizumab group and 83.3% in the cCRT group. The 1‑year PFS rates were 65.5% with camrelizumab versus 47.4% with cCRT (P = 0.029). Median PFS was 24.0 months versus 11.8 months, and median OS was not reached versus 23.9 months (P = 0.042). Exploratory biomarker analyses indicated that patients with lower baseline systemic inflammatory indices, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio <2.8 and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio <207.0, and those with a decline in lactate dehydrogenase at week 12 after CRT, derived greater benefit from camrelizumab. The OS benefit was also more evident in patients with Ki-67 ≤80%. Toxicities in the camrelizumab group were manageable, with a low incidence of severe immune-related adverse events (4.8%), and radiation pneumonitis rates were comparable between groups. Taken together, induction camrelizumab combined with chemotherapy, followed by CRT and camrelizumab consolidation, significantly improved survival outcomes in LS-SCLC, with a manageable safety profile, warranting further validation for this aggressive malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative anxiety is highly prevalent in patients undergoing thoracoscopic lung resection, adversely affecting postoperative recovery. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulatory intervention with demonstrated efficacy in various psychiatric and stress-related conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of taVNS in reducing perioperative anxiety in this population. METHODS: This single-center, parallel-group, randomized, double-blind, superiority trial was conducted at the Department of Anesthesiology and Thoracic Surgery, the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University between October 10, 2024, and April 30, 2025. A total of 176 eligible patients aged ≥18 years with ASA physical status I-III and scheduled for elective thoracoscopic lung resection were enrolled. Patients with neuropsychiatric disorders, auricular lesions, severe cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, implanted electronic devices, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score <15, long-term psychotropic medication use or postural tachycardia syndrome were excluded. All participants were randomly allocated to receive four sessions of either active taVNS or sham taVNS. Stimulation was delivered via the auricular branch of the vagus nerve at the cymba conchae of the left ear at four predefined perioperative time points: the afternoon before surgery, the morning of surgery, immediately after tracheal extubation, and the afternoon of the first postoperative day. The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative anxiety, assessed from the initiation of the first taVNS session through 3 days postoperatively. All participants, healthcare providers, outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to group assignment during the whole study. RESULTS: A total of 176 patients were randomly assigned, with 88 participants in the active taVNS group and 88 in the sham taVNS group. After excluding 2 patients (1 patient from each group) who were transferred to the ICU postoperatively, a total of 174 patients (median age, 58 years; 105 women [60.4%]) completed the study and were analysed for the primary outcome, including 87 patients in each group. The incidence of perioperative anxiety was significantly lower in the active taVNS group than in the sham taVNS group (50.6% vs. 73.6%; relative risk [RR], 0.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41-0.85; χ2 = 9.76; P = 0.002). Compared with sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with reductions in anxiety and depression scores, postoperative pain intensity, and physiological stress indices and improvement in sleep quality and overall postoperative recovery. No severe adverse events were observed in either group. The main mild adverse reactions included nausea, vomiting, local tingling, dizziness and headache, and the incidence of adverse events was similar between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Four perioperative sessions of taVNS applied to the left cymba conchae significantly reduced the incidence of perioperative anxiety in patients undergoing thoracoscopic lung resection and were additionally associated with improvements in depressive symptoms, stress burden, sleep quality, and pain outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Register Identifier: ChiCTR2400090542 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: While accelerated hypofractionated radiotherapy has increasingly been adopted in the multidisciplinary management of locally-advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ineligible for concurrent chemotherapy, there is a paucity of randomized prospective evidence guiding utilization. Given the marked heterogeneity in the presentations of locally-advanced NSCLC, the American Radium Society (ARS) Thoracic Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) Panel evaluated the appropriateness of accelerated hypofractionation in the context of multidisciplinary management. METHODS: Five clinical variants representing manifestations of locally-advanced NSCLC were developed by the 15-member multidisciplinary ARS Thoracic AUC panel. The English-language medical literature was formally reviewed from 2010-2025 and scrutinized for prospective clinical trials utilizing accelerated hypofractionation for concurrent chemotherapy ineligible patients. All case variants were evaluated with respect to use of radiation technique, radiation fractionation, and utilization of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy with Modified Delphi methodology. Consensus recommendations were reviewed and approved by the ARS Executive Committee and subject to public comment. RESULTS: The literature review identified 228 articles, of which there were 14 prospective trials/registries including nine Phase I-II trials, four prospective registries, and one randomized Phase III trial. There was consensus that it is appropriate to utilize intensity modulated radiation therapy and proton therapy across presentations of locally-advanced NSCLC, with the aim of constraining the lung V20Gy<30% and heart V40Gy<20% with accelerated hypofractionation. When utilizing 15-fraction accelerated hypofractionation for disease abutting the esophagus or brachial plexus, there was consensus that it is inappropriate to exceed doses of 45-55 Gy. With respect to PD-L1 immunotherapy, there was consensus that consolidative immunotherapy after definitive radiation therapy is appropriate, but that concurrent immunotherapy is inappropriate. There was panel consensus that it may be appropriate to utilize induction PD-L1 immunotherapy prior to radiation therapy in cases of bulky or N3 disease to test disease biology. Across variants, there was consensus that conventionally fractionated radiotherapy to 60 Gy in 30 fractions remains appropriate. CONCLUSIONS: The ARS Thoracic AUC Panel has provided consensus case-based guidelines on the multidisciplinary management of locally-advanced NSCLC ineligible for concurrent chemotherapy reflecting the heterogeneity of disease presentation in this population. In absence of randomized prospective data demonstrating superiority of accelerated hypofractionation, conventionally fractionated radiotherapy remains an appropriate option.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thermal ablation (TA) is a safe and feasible alternative for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. However, data on the clinical efficacy of TA in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) are scarce. This study aimed to explore the clinical efficacy of TA plus chemotherapy (CHT) in treating SCLC. METHODS: This is a population-based retrospective cohort study based on the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database. We collected data from the SEER database for 51,273 SCLC patients who received CHT from 2000 to 2019. Using propensity score matching (PSM), we balanced covariate differences between two treatment groups: CHT alone and TA plus CHT. Kaplan-Meier survival curves for overall survival (OS) and lung cancer-specific survival (LCSS) were generated. Cox regression analysis was conducted to assess independent prognostic indicators. RESULTS: After PSM, the TA + CHT group exhibited superior OS and LCSS compared to the CHT-only group. Age subgroup analysis revealed that for patients aged ≥70 years, TA + CHT resulted in improved OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone. For patients <70 years, a survival benefit was observed, but the difference was not statistically significant. Tumor size subgroup analysis showed that for patients with tumor sizes of 0-3 cm, TA + CHT led to superior OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, while no statistically significant differences were observed in other tumor size subgroups. N stage subgroup analysis indicated that for N0 and N1 patients, TA + CHT had better OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, with no statistically significant differences in the N2 and N3 subgroups. Multivariable analysis indicated that TA + CHT was an independent favorable prognostic indicator for both OS and LCSS. CONCLUSIONS: TA + CHT may be a promising treatment option for patients with SCLC, especially those aged ≥70 years with tumor size ≤3 cm, and N0-1 disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Randomized evidence for immune checkpoint inhibition in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer has progressed from pathological response to mature survival outcomes. We examined exploratory directional alignment across endpoints and quantified clinical yield, treatment burden, and the extent of perioperative therapy delivery. METHODS: We synthesized 20 peer-reviewed reports from 12 parent randomized trials, including 8,197 unique participants and 13 eligible randomized treatment comparisons. The parent trial was the analysis unit, and the latest compatible report replaced earlier estimates for each time-to-event outcome. Direct randomized comparisons were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models. We reconstructed cumulative event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) evidence, estimated absolute differences, performed exploratory trial-level cross-endpoint analyses, and pooled the proportion of experimental-arm patients who started postoperative study treatment. RESULTS: Across seven trials, treatment initiated before surgery reduced EFS events by 41% (HR, 0.59; 95% CI: 0.53-0.66; I2 = 12%). Five trials showed a 32% reduction in death (HR, 0.68; 95% CI: 0.58-0.80; I2 = 0%). Per 100 randomized patients, preoperative-start therapy produced 31 additional major pathological responses (95% CI: 24-39), 22 additional pathological complete responses (95% CI: 16-27), and 4 additional patients who underwent or attempted curative-intent surgery (95% CI: 1-7). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events increased by approximately 4 per 100 patients (95% CI: 0-8). In exploratory analyses, larger pCR improvements tended to accompany lower EFS HRs (Spearman ρ = -0.67; p = 0.098; k = 7), and EFS and OS estimates were directionally aligned (ρ = 0.95; p = 0.051; k = 4). In six perioperative trials, 69.7% (95% CI: 65.5%-73.7%) of randomized experimental-arm patients started postoperative study treatment. CONCLUSION: ICI-containing strategies initiated before surgery improve pathological response, EFS, and OS in resectable NSCLC. Approximately 70% of patients assigned to perioperative experimental arms started postoperative study treatment; this descriptive treatment-delivery finding does not establish whether postoperative ICI can be safely omitted. Prospective response- and residual-risk-guided randomized trials are required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are a major cause of morbidity after lung resection, particularly in older adults. Following extubation, noninvasive respiratory support strategies are increasingly used to prevent respiratory deterioration, but the role of prophylactic high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) in this setting remains uncertain. METHODS: In this single-center, open-label randomized controlled trial, patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy or segmentectomy for stage I-IIIa non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomized to HFNC or conventional oxygen therapy (COT). The primary outcome was PPC severity during hospitalization, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression; the incidence of clinically relevant PPCs (grade ≥ 2) was also compared between groups. Secondary outcomes included longitudinal respiratory symptoms (mMRC, LCQ-MC, sCSS) and symptom-related functional interference (MDASI-LC), analyzed using mixed-effects models. RESULTS: A total of 210 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (HFNC, n = 104; COT, n = 106). HFNC reduced PPC severity (ordinal OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.91; P = 0.022) and moderate-to-severe PPCs (23.1% vs. 39.6%; absolute risk difference, -15.6%; 95% CI, -28.0% to -3.2%; P = 0.010). HFNC was associated with a lower burden of clinically relevant PPCs. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. No differences were observed in physiological outcomes or length of stay. CONCLUSION: In older adults undergoing lung resection, prophylactic HFNC reduced in-hospital PPC burden and was associated with more favorable early postoperative respiratory recovery. These findings suggest that prophylactic HFNC may provide benefit as a potential preventive respiratory support option in selected older or higher-risk postoperative patients, although routine prophylactic use in all patients undergoing lung resection is not supported by the present findings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was approved by the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2200063161) on 01 Sep 2022 and the first patient was enrolled after pre-registration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although nasogastric decompression, nasojejunal feeding, and abdominal drainage tubes are not routinely recommended in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) guidelines for gastrectomy, evidence regarding the avoidance of any inserted tubes after laparoscopic gastrectomy remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term feasibility and clinical outcomes of an ERAS-tubeless protocol in gastric cancer patients undergoing non-high-risk laparoscopy-assisted gastrectomy. METHODS: At a high-volume center, eligible patients of gastric cancer (cT1-4N0-3M0) who lacked protocol-defined high-risk features were enrolled in this prospective non-randomized controlled study. Patients were allocated to either the ERAS-tubeless group or the ERAS-tube group at a predefined 1:1 ratio according to a team-level allocation protocol. All patients underwent laparoscopy-assisted gastrectomy following strict and consistent quality control standards and received distinct ERAS-based postoperative tube-management strategies. The primary outcome was postoperative hospital stay, and secondary outcomes included postoperative quality of life scores and the incidence of complications. RESULTS: Between March 2023 and September 2024, 220 patients were allocated, and 205 were included in the per-protocol population after post-allocation exclusions. The ERAS-tubeless group had a shorter mean postoperative hospital stay (6.0 vs. 7.3 days; P < 0.001). After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple comparisons, QoR-15 scores remained significantly higher on postoperative days 1 and 3. For the EORTC QLQ-C30, significant between-group differences persisted in global health and QoL, emotional functioning, and social functioning domains. No increase in the incidence of early postoperative complications was observed; however, the study was underpowered to exclude rare but serious adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: In non-high-risk patients with gastric cancer, implementation of the ERAS-tubeless strategy following laparoscopy-assisted gastrectomy under a rigorous surgical quality control system can facilitate postoperative recovery, enhance patient experience, and not increase the risk of early postoperative complications, which warrants further validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Phase 3 MARIPOSA-2 study showed that amivantamab, a bispecific antibody with immune cell-directing activity, plus chemotherapy significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared with chemotherapy alone in participants with common epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), whose disease had progressed on osimertinib monotherapy. We conducted a post hoc analysis to assess clinical outcomes in the Asian subgroup of participants from MARIPOSA-2 (NCT04988295). METHODS: Participants were randomised 2:2:1 to amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy, chemotherapy alone, or amivantamab-chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was PFS by blinded independent central review (BICR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1 (RECIST 1.1). Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, and safety. Due to mid-study modifications to the amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy dosing schedule, follow-up of this group is ongoing. We present results for the amivantamab-chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy arms in the Asian subgroup. RESULTS: There were 190 participants in the Asian subgroup, 63 in the amivantamab-chemotherapy group and 127 in the chemotherapy group. At a median follow-up of 9.5 months, median PFS in the amivantamab-chemotherapy arm was 6.8 vs. 4.2 months in the chemotherapy arm [hazard ratio (HR) 0.54, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.37-0.81; nominal P=0.002]. The ORR was 66% and 32%, respectively (odds ratio 4.0, 95% CI: 2.1-7.7; nominal P<0.001) and median intracranial PFS was 12.5 and 8.5 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.34-1.00; nominal P=0.049). The safety profile in the Asian subgroup was in line with the overall MARIPOSA-2 population. CONCLUSIONS: Amivantamab-chemotherapy demonstrated superior PFS vs. chemotherapy in Asian patients. Amivantamab-chemotherapy provides an effective option for patients whose disease had progressed on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

papers.abstract_en: Epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) disease biology may differ from EGFR-wild type NSCLC, with an increased risk of distant metastases in unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC. Osimertinib is an established first treatment for patients with EGFRm advanced NSCLC, effectively treating EGFRm tumours. The phase III LAURA study, which assessed the efficacy and safety of osimertinib for patients with locally advanced, unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC who completed chemoradiotherapy (CRT) without disease progression, demonstrated a statistically significant improvement with osimertinib in progression-free survival (PFS), with a median PFS of 39.1 months, versus 5.6 months with placebo. The safety profile was as expected based on the known profiles of osimertinib and CRT. On the basis of the LAURA results, osimertinib has now been approved for the treatment of unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC. Given the implementation of the LAURA regimen in multiple countries, this podcast highlights the potential challenges that must be considered by healthcare professionals when administering osimertinib in clinical practice, and how these may be mitigated. Considerations of the impact of the 'treat-to-progression' approach, a paradigm shift for the treatment of stage III unresectable NSCLC, and patient-centred care, including the importance of shared decision-making, will also be discussed. Overall, continuous systemic treatment post-CRT may be key to improving long-term outcomes and represents a mindset shift for both healthcare professionals and patients. Therefore, we may need to consider unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC as a chronic disease, requiring long-term treatment to maintain suppression of disease.The podcast and transcript can be viewed below the abstract of the online version of the manuscript. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics are increasingly used to analyze imaging and multisource data in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the directness and clinical maturity of the available evidence remain uncertain. This narrative review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, and indirect evidence across diagnostic classification, prognostic prediction, treatment-associated outcomes, and lesion segmentation. METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted to identify human studies evaluating AI, deep learning (DL), radiomics, or machine learning within imaging-based or imaging-integrated workflows. Studies were selected according to clinical relevance, directness of SCLC evidence, methodological strength, and reporting completeness, and were classified as SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, or indirect/transferable evidence. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Direct SCLC-specific evidence was strongest for multicenter computed tomography (CT)-based prognostic models and lesion segmentation, whereas diagnostic classification relied mainly on mixed cohorts or public image-level datasets. Treatment-response models showed preliminary value but were predominantly retrospective and lacked prospective clinical validation. Retrospective studies suggested associations between model-derived risk scores and outcomes following prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI), but did not establish treatment-benefit prediction. Pathomic and radiogenomic analyses also identified associations between quantitative features, immune-cell infiltration, genomic alterations, and treatment response; these findings remain hypothesis-generating. Interpretation is limited by small SCLC cohorts, retrospective single-center designs, non-independent image-level analyses, and limited external validation and interpretability. CONCLUSIONS: AI and radiomics show potential in SCLC, particularly for CT-based prognosis and segmentation. However, treatment-response prediction, non-invasive subtype classification, and clinical decision support remain investigational and require prospective multicenter validation and patient-level external evaluation before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: For patients with resectable locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), surgical resection preceded by neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nICT) has become the standard treatment strategy. However, the triple physiological burden imposed by chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and ongoing tumor metabolism may compromise functional reserve and increase surgical risk. Identifying patients at high risk for postoperative complications remains a critical challenge in perioperative management. This study aimed to characterize dynamic changes in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue during nICT, to identify independent predictors of postoperative complications, and to evaluate the incremental predictive value of dynamic body composition metrics over established clinical variables. METHODS: This retrospective study included 160 patients with resectable NSCLC who underwent surgical resection following nICT between June 2024 and December 2025. Skeletal muscle index (SMI), skeletal muscle density (SMD), visceral adipose tissue (VAT), and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) were quantified at the L3 vertebral level on computed tomography (CT) images obtained before and after treatment. Dynamic changes (Δ) were calculated as the difference between pre-treatment and post-treatment values. The primary outcome was postoperative complications of Clavien-Dindo (CD) grade ≥II. Three predictive models were constructed and compared using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: Following nICT, skeletal muscle metrics decreased significantly (median ΔSMI, -0.54 cm2/m2; P=0.01; median ΔSMD, -0.90 HU; P=0.003), while adipose tissue areas increased significantly (median ΔVAT, 9.54 cm2; P<0.001; median ΔSAT, 8.06 cm2; P<0.001). No significant correlation was observed between ΔSMI and ΔVAT (Spearman ρ=0.087; P=0.27), indicating divergent and independent metabolic trajectories. Of 160 patients, 58 (36.3%) developed CD grade ≥ II complications. Among the four dynamic body-composition measures, each evaluated in a separate multivariable model, only ΔSMI remained significantly associated with postoperative complications [adjusted odds ratio (OR) =0.806; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.721-0.900; P<0.001], whereas ΔSMD, ΔVAT, and ΔSAT did not. Traditional assessments, including body mass index (BMI) change, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, pulmonary function, and systemic inflammatory and nutritional indices, likewise showed no significant associations. Adding ΔSMI to the clinical model significantly improved AUC from 0.595 to 0.710 (ΔAUC =0.115; P=0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic loss of skeletal muscle during nICT, as assessed on routine CT images, was independently associated with postoperative complications in patients with resectable NSCLC. Compared with baseline body-composition parameters and conventional clinical indices, longitudinal change in SMI (ΔSMI) provided better discrimination of perioperative risk. Because ΔSMI can be derived from CT scans already obtained for treatment-response assessment, it may serve as a practical, low-burden imaging biomarker to support preoperative risk stratification and identify patients who may benefit from targeted prehabilitation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (niVATS) avoids endotracheal intubation and one-lung mechanical ventilation. Whether this translates into clinically meaningful benefits compared with intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) requires comparative studies. Evidence from European centers, particularly for major pulmonary resections, remains limited. We evaluated technical feasibility and perioperative outcomes in a selected European niVATS cohort. METHODS: This retrospective single-center observational study included consecutive patients selected to undergo niVATS between May 2018 and February 2025. The primary endpoint was intraoperative conversion to intubated anesthesia. Secondary endpoints included postoperative complications, chest tube duration, length of stay, reoperation, and 30-day mortality. RESULTS: A total of 163 patients were included. Median age was 67 years and median body mass index (BMI) was 24 kg/m2. Anatomical lung resections were performed in 77 patients (47.2%), including 50 lobectomies and 27 segmentectomies. Conversion to intubated anesthesia occurred in 6 patients (3.7%). Prolonged air leak was observed in 21 patients (12.9%), pneumonia in 5 (3.1%), and reoperation in 6 (3.7%). Thirty-day mortality was 1.2%. Median chest tube duration and hospital stay were 3 and 5 days, respectively. Conversion was more frequently observed among patients undergoing lobectomy and among those with a higher BMI. CONCLUSIONS: niVATS is feasible in selected patients across a broad spectrum of thoracic procedures in a high-volume European center. Lobectomy and increasing BMI are associated with a higher likelihood of conversion and should be considered during patient selection and perioperative planning. These descriptive findings do not establish comparative safety or clinical benefit versus intubated VATS; prospective comparative studies are required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The INT0139 trial [2009] raised concerns about the safety of pneumonectomy after chemoradiation due to high perioperative mortality rates. Recent clinical trials have supported the use of neoadjuvant treatment as a viable option for stage Ib or greater lung cancer. We hypothesized that neoadjuvant treatment does not increase perioperative mortality risk in patients undergoing pneumonectomy. METHODS: Adult patients with nonmetastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) from the 2004-2021 National Cancer Database undergoing pneumonectomy were analyzed in a retrospective cohort study. Exclusions included missing study variables, non-adenocarcinoma/squamous histology and pneumonectomy after neoadjuvant radiation alone. Multivariate logistic regression analyzed 30- and 90-day mortality and included laterality and neoadjuvant treatment interactions. RESULTS: Of 14,522 patients, 58.6% underwent right pneumonectomy and 41.4% underwent left pneumonectomy. Neoadjuvant treatment was received by 14.9% (systemic therapy alone: 1,008; systemic therapy + radiation: 1,156). The 90-day mortality was higher for right versus left pneumonectomy (17.2% vs. 9.8%, P<0.001). Neoadjuvant therapy was not associated with higher 90-day mortality compared to surgery alone (10.4% vs. 13%, P=0.04). Independent predictors of mortality included right-sided pneumonectomy [odds ratio (OR) =2.01, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.78-2.28], advanced age (OR =1.05, 95% CI: 1.04-1.06), and Charlson-Deyo index ≥ 3 (OR =1.98, 95% CI: 1.53-2.57). Interaction analysis showed no increased risk with neoadjuvant therapy for either side. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis reiterates known elevated risk associated with right pneumonectomy but disputes the dogma that neoadjuvant treatment increases the risk of pneumonectomy, suggesting that neoadjuvant treatment is not a contraindication to receipt of pneumonectomy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a heterogeneous disease, and the role of surgery within multimodality treatment remains controversial. With the emergence of immunotherapy, there is a need to re-evaluate surgical outcomes in real-world populations. This study compares overall survival (OS) between surgical and non-surgical approaches for stage IIIA NSCLC from a multicenter cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 598 stage IIIA NSCLC patients diagnosed between January 1, 2010, and June 30, 2021, across 21 Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) hospitals. Patients were categorized into surgical and non-surgical groups; the surgical group was further divided into surgery alone, surgery first (adjuvant therapy), and surgery later (neoadjuvant or perioperative therapy). RESULTS: The surgical group had higher 5-year OS (52.6% vs. 30.8%, P<0.001) and longer median survival (5.77 vs. 2.17 years). All surgical subgroups were independently associated with reduced mortality after adjusting for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, Charlson Comorbidity Score (CCS), and race: surgery later [adjusted hazard ratio (AHR) =0.50; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.34-0.74], surgery alone (AHR =0.58; 95% CI: 0.39-0.89), and surgery first (AHR =0.48; 95% CI: 0.37-0.62). Age >80 years (AHR =1.65; 95% CI: 1.07-2.55; P=0.02) and male sex (AHR =1.64; 95% CI: 1.30-2.06; P<0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Surgery, when integrated into multimodal treatment, is associated with significantly improved survival in stage IIIA NSCLC. These findings support continued consideration of surgery in appropriately selected patients and highlight the need for prospective studies to clarify its role in NSCLC management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophagectomy remains an effective treatment for esophageal cancer but is associated with severe postoperative complications, in which nutritional status plays a critical role. The optimal route for enteral feeding remains uncertain. To address this uncertainty, we compared the short-term clinical outcomes of the two approaches and exploratorily analyzed the differences in gut microbiota. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients who underwent minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) between July 2018 and June 2021. Primary outcomes were surgery-related complications (including anastomotic leakage, anastomotic stenosis, pneumonia, respiratory failure, cardiac events, chylothorax, intestinal fistula and bowel obstruction) and catheter-related outcomes (including occlusion, accidental removal, displacement and retention time). Baseline data were extracted from medical records. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to control for potential confounders. Intestinal fluid and fecal samples were collected after enteral nutrition for 16S ribosomal DNA (16S rDNA) sequencing. RESULTS: After PSM, a total of 381 patients (nasoduodenal tube: 282; feeding jejunostomy: 153) was finally included. The feeding jejunostomy group exhibited a higher incidence of pneumonia (21.49% vs. 33.99%, P=0.007), respiratory failure (3.07% vs. 13.07%, P<0.001), anastomotic stenosis (1.32% vs. 5.23%, P=0.03) and bowel obstruction (0% vs. 2.16%, P=0.03). Nasoduodenal tube placement was associated with more accidental removal (13.16% vs. 0.65%, P<0.001) and catheter displacement (13.60% vs. 6.54%, P=0.03). The catheter retention time {37 [interquartile range (IQR): 15-40] days vs. 39 (IQR: 37-42) days, P<0.001} was also shorter in nasoduodenal tube group. CONCLUSIONS: In this study, nasoduodenal tube placement was associated with a higher incidence of catheter-related complications, whereas feeding jejunostomy was linked to more surgery-related complications. Nasoduodenal tube placement also showed potential functional advantages for the gut microbiome. However, future multi-center randomized controlled trials are still needed to minimize potential confounders and validate the differences between the two enteral nutrition routes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Post-discharge venous thromboembolism prophylaxis is conditionally recommended after thoracic cancer operation, but real-world use and associated outcomes across procedures and operative approaches remain poorly characterized. STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective Epic Cosmos cohort study of adults undergoing lung or esophageal cancer resection from 2016-2025. Post-discharge prophylaxis was defined as prophylactic-dose anticoagulation prescribed within 7 days of discharge. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using 1:3 propensity-score matching stratified by procedure and operative approach. RESULTS: Among 157,619 patients (14,277 esophagectomy; 143,342 lung resection), 11.15% and 1.48%, respectively, received post-discharge prophylaxis. After open esophagectomy, prophylaxis was associated with lower DVT (1.23% vs 2.63%; p=0.039), PE (0.46% vs 1.44%; p=0.047), and mortality (1.70% vs 5.20%; p<0.001), without significantly increased bleeding. Findings were similar after minimally invasive esophagectomy: DVT 0.32% vs 1.46% (p=0.003), PE 0.21% vs 0.89% (p=0.034), and mortality 1.28% vs 3.20% (p=0.003). After open lung resection, prophylaxis was associated with lower PE and mortality but higher bleeding and healthcare use. After minimally invasive lung resection, thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ, while bleeding and healthcare use were higher. Enoxaparin accounted for 79.35% of prophylaxis prescriptions; thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ between apixaban and enoxaparin. CONCLUSIONS: Associations between post-discharge thromboprophylaxis and outcomes differed across thoracic procedures and operative approaches. Favorable associations after esophagectomy contrasted with less consistent lung resection findings, supporting prospective studies to define procedure- and risk-specific prophylaxis strategies.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effect of preoperative single-injection paravertebral block using liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture versus ropivacaine on cumulative postoperative opioid consumption in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (wedge resection, segmentectomy, or lobectomy) between January 2024 and February 2026. Patients received an ultrasound-guided single-injection paravertebral block with either 0.5% ropivacaine (20 mL) or a mixture of 1.3% liposomal bupivacaine (10 mL) and 0.5% standard bupivacaine (10 mL). The primary outcome was cumulative postoperative opioid consumption throughout the hospitalization, delivered via patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) and converted to oral morphine milligram equivalents. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, time to first PCA request, postoperative adverse events, and length of stay. Propensity score matching (1:2) was performed to balance baseline clinical and intraoperative characteristics. RESULTS: Among 492 eligible patients, 331 received ropivacaine and 161 received liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine combination. After matching, 210 and 108 patients were included in the ropivacaine and liposomal bupivacaine groups, respectively. The median cumulative postoperative opioid consumption was lower in the liposomal bupivacaine group (92.1 mg [IQR, 59.1-122.3]) than in the ropivacaine group (226.2 mg [IQR, 170.2-260.0]), with a median difference of 128.2 mg (95% CI, 111.0-143.9; P < 0.001). The liposomal bupivacaine group was also associated with lower resting and movement pain scores at 24 and 48 hours postoperatively, a longer time to first PCA press (26.0 vs. 6.0 hours; P < 0.001), and a lower incidence of postoperative dizziness (21.3% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.017). CONCLUSION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, preoperative single-injection paravertebral blockade with liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture was associated with lower cumulative postoperative opioid consumption and lower early postoperative pain scores than ropivacaine.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Wide use of low-dose chest CT detects more early NSCLC, though recurrence (mostly extracranial distant metastasis) still occurs. This study aimed to establish and validate computed tomography (CT) radiomics models that can be used for predicting the risk of extracranial distant metastasis (EDM) after radical resection in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (e-NSCLC). METHODS: This retrospective study included 312 patients with e-NSCLC who underwent radical surgery at Shandong Cancer Hospital from 2014 to 2019. The cases were randomly divided into a training set (n=200) and a validation set (n=112). The study excluded patients who received neoadjuvant therapy, had interrupted follow-up, or died of non-tumor-related causes. The patients were followed up for an average of 30.6 months after the first postoperative CT examination. This study defined EDM as distant metastasis in other organs other than brain metastasis after surgery, and accounted for 78.6% of all metastatic cases. The region of interest (ROI) was delineated, and the radiomics features were selected by using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression models to construct radiomics signatures. The association between the radiomics signature and the occurrence of EDM was also evaluated. A combined nomogram incorporating the selected radiomics and clinical-pathological predictors was constructed using multivariable regression. The concordance index (C-index) was used to evaluate the performance of the model. To determine the clinical effectiveness of nomogram in radiomics, the decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed. RESULTS: A total of 75 patients (24.0%) experienced metastasis, with EDM accounting for 78.6%. In the overall cohort, radiomics signature were significantly associated with the occurrence of the EDM. The discrimination performance of the radiomics nomogram is significantly better than the clinical-pathologic nomogram (P<0.001), with the C-indexes 0.818 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.780-0.856] and 0.823 (95% CI: 0.769-0.877) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Analysis of the calibration and decision curves indicated that the comprehensive nomogram was superior to the clinical-pathological and radiomics nomogram in predicting EDM survival. CONCLUSIONS: CT radiomics features have the potential to predict postoperative EDM and may assist in preliminarily identifying patients at high metastatic risk, which could provide a reference for individualized postoperative adjuvant decision-making in e-NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is the standard of care for early-stage lung cancer, yet 20-30% of patients still experience moderate-to-severe acute postoperative pain. A wide range of perioperative analgesic strategies-regional blocks, systemic adjuncts, cryoanalgesia, and multimodal combinations-have been evaluated, but their comparative effects on clinically meaningful endpoints such as postoperative complications remain uncertain. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of perioperative analgesic strategies for VATS lobectomy. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (PROSPERO CRD420251186565), following the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from 1 January 2010 to 26 June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool per outcome. Postoperative complications were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) estimation. Studies were grouped by intervention type for subgroup analysis. Sensitivity was assessed with leave-one-out analysis. RESULTS: Seven trials (n=505) met inclusion criteria. The evidence base was clinically heterogeneous: included comparisons encompassed regional technique variations [paravertebral block (PVB), serratus anterior plane block (SAPB), intercostal nerve block (ICNB), and their combinations], systemic adjunctive analgesics (nefopam), and intercostal cryoanalgesia. Only three trials reported usable complication data for quantitative synthesis (n=245). The overall pooled RR for postoperative complications was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.65-1.08; P=0.18), but this estimate was dominated by a single trial (Koliakos 2025, 75.2% weight). Between-study heterogeneity was absent (I2=0%, τ2=0; Q=0.39, df =2, P=0.82). Subgroup analyses by intervention class (regional techniques, systemic adjuncts, cryoanalgesia) did not yield statistically significant pooled estimates. Leave-one-out exclusion of the largest study shifted the point estimate to RR 0.95 (95% CI: 0.57-1.58), confirming strong dependence on a single trial. With fewer than 10 studies, formal publication bias assessment was not performed. CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence on perioperative analgesic strategies for VATS lobectomy consists of small, heterogeneous trials comparing diverse interventions. No single strategy has been shown to consistently reduce postoperative complications. The evidence base is insufficient to guide clinical practice. Adequately powered, multicentre RCTs with standardised interventions, composite complication endpoints, and extended follow-up are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Thoracogastric airway fistula (TGAF) is a life-threatening complication following esophagectomy with gastric conduit interposition. While early-onset TGAF has been well characterized, late-onset TGAF, which occurs months to years after surgery, remains underrecognized and lacks evidence-based diagnostic and management frameworks. This narrative review aims to synthesize current literature to address several high-priority clinical questions: which features should raise suspicion of lateonset TGAF; what is the optimal diagnostic pathway integrating imaging and endoscopy; and how to select between endoscopic and surgical intervention. METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed from database inception to May 2026 using combinations of keywords related to TGAF and relevant etiological and therapeutic terms. Reference lists of included articles and relevant reviews were manually screened. Only peer-reviewed English-language publications were considered. Given the rarity and heterogeneity of late-onset TGAF, high-quality prospective studies are lacking, and a systematic review with meta-analysis is not feasible. We therefore adopted a narrative synthesis approach. KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: The evidence base for late-onset TGAF is limited to case reports, small series, and a few cohort studies, with no randomized trials identified. Diagnostic delay is common, driven by nonspecific symptoms and overlap with tumor progression. The pathogenesis is multifactorial, with peptic ulceration as the bestsupported mechanism. Management options include conservative support, endoscopic stenting or occluder devices, and surgical repair, though treatment decisions are guided largely by patient physiology, fistula characteristics, and institutional expertise rather than by comparative data. Long-term outcomes remain poorly characterized. CONCLUSIONS: This review presents an initial framework for managing late-onset TGAF. A high index of suspicion should be maintained in any post-esophagectomy patient presenting with recurrent pneumonia, chronic cough, or unexplained weight loss. Diagnostic workup should proceed with contrast esophagram and chest computed tomography (CT), followed by confirmatory bronchoscopy and gastroscopy. Endoscopic stenting is appropriate as firstline therapy in most patients, whereas surgical repair should be reserved for those with adequate physiological reserve and favorable local tissue conditions. The limited evidence base underscore the urgent need for prospective multicenter registries to establish standardized diagnostic algorithms and treatment guidelines for this rare but devastating complication.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary nodules detected during postoperative surveillance in breast cancer survivors present a diagnostic challenge because imaging findings alone often cannot reliably distinguish pulmonary metastases from primary lung cancer. Surgical resection provides definitive pathological diagnosis while simultaneously enabling biomarker reassessment in metastatic lesions. This study evaluated the diagnostic value and clinical significance of pulmonary resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules in patients with prior breast cancer. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 33 pulmonary resections performed in 32 consecutive patients with a history of breast cancer who underwent pulmonary resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules between 2016 and 2025. Clinicopathological findings, imaging characteristics, perioperative outcomes, and receptor discordance between primary breast tumors and pulmonary metastatic lesions were analyzed. Paired biomarker data were available for 18 patients with pulmonary metastases. RESULTS: Final pathological diagnoses included metastatic breast cancer in 23 lesions (69.7%), primary lung cancer in 9 lesions (27.3%), and benign disease in 1 lesion (3.0%), indicating that more than one-quarter of lesions suspected preoperatively to represent pulmonary metastases were actually primary lung cancers. Most procedures were performed using video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (87.9%). Among patients with paired biomarker data, substantial discordance in hormone receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) expression was observed, including frequent conversion between HER2-0 and HER2-low categories. Biomarker reassessment resulted in modification of subsequent systemic treatment in three patients. Perioperative outcomes were favorable, with no operative mortality and low postoperative morbidity. CONCLUSIONS: Surgical resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules in selected patients with prior breast cancer provides definitive pathological diagnosis, appropriate local treatment, and sufficient tissue for biomarker reassessment. Histological confirmation should be considered when imaging findings remain inconclusive because pulmonary nodules in breast cancer survivors are not necessarily metastatic disease. Biomarker reassessment may directly influence individualized systemic treatment strategies in the HER2-low era.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have demonstrated substantial efficacy in advanced ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but evidence for their use in the neoadjuvant setting remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant ALK-targeted therapy and chemotherapy-based neoadjuvant treatment in surgically treated patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 20 patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by curative-intent surgery at the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Hunan Cancer Hospital, between October 2018 and April 2025. Patients were retrospectively classified into an ALK-TKI group (n=13) and a chemotherapy-based group (n=7) according to the neoadjuvant regimen received. A comparative analysis assessed radiological response, pathological response, postoperative complications, adverse events, and survival outcomes between the 2 groups after neoadjuvant therapy. RESULTS: The baseline characteristics of the 2 groups were comparable without statistically significant differences. Among the 13 patients in the ALK-TKI group, 9 achieved partial response (PR) and 4 had stable disease (SD), resulting in an objective response rate (ORR) of 69.2%. Among the 7 patients in the chemotherapy-based group, 3 achieved PR and 4 had SD, resulting in an ORR of 42.9% (P=0.35). Six patients (46.2%) in the ALK-TKI group and one patient (14.3%) in the chemotherapy-based group achieved major pathological response (MPR) (P=0.32). Four patients (30.8%) in the ALK-TKI group and one patient (14.3%) in the chemotherapy-based group achieved pathological complete response (pCR) (P=0.61). The proportion of patients with ypN0 disease was significantly higher in the ALK-TKI group than in the chemotherapy-based group (11/13 vs. 3/7, P=0.043), and the extent of pathological nodal downstaging was also greater in the ALK-TKI group (P=0.008). There were no significant differences between the 2 groups in the incidence of adverse events, grade ≥3 adverse events, postoperative complications, surgical approach, operative time, blood loss, thoracic drainage duration, or postoperative hospital stay. Kaplan-Meier analyses showed nonsignificant numerical trends toward improved overall survival and recurrence-free survival in the ALK-TKI group. However, these findings were based on a small number of recurrence and death events and should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant ALK-TKI therapy showed numerically higher radiological and pathological response rates and a significantly higher ypN0 rate and greater pathological nodal downstaging relative to the baseline clinical nodal stage compared with chemotherapy-based neoadjuvant therapy. No statistically significant differences in the observed safety or perioperative outcomes were identified between the groups.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leakage (AL) after esophagectomy is a serious complication for which early physiological signals remain limited. We conducted a hypothesis-generating analysis of whether routinely reported electrocardiographic QRS measurements were associated with AL during the perioperative period. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 292 of 1,441 patients undergoing esophagectomy who had an index 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) from day -1 through postoperative day 1. ECG acquisition followed routine clinical practice rather than a study protocol. QRS duration and frontal-plane QRS axis were retained after descriptive screening of the continuous ECG measurements available in the analytic extract. They were entered into a two-variable logistic model, followed by a sensitivity model additionally adjusting for seven clinical characteristics. Timing-stratified associations and same-cohort model discrimination were also examined. RESULTS: AL occurred in 29 of 292 patients (9.9%). Patients with AL had a shorter QRS duration (median, 86 vs. 92 ms; P = 0.016) and a more leftward QRS axis (4 degrees vs. 27 degrees; P = 0.006). In the two-variable model, standardized odds ratios (ORs) were 0.378 (95% CI, 0.178-0.801) for QRS duration and 0.501 (0.323-0.779) for QRS axis. In the sensitivity model, the corresponding ORs were 0.359 (0.170-0.761) and 0.486 (0.299-0.789). The QRS-axis association was stronger preoperatively, whereas the QRS-duration association was stronger from day 0 through postoperative day 1. Median repeated-cross-validation AUCs were 0.702 for the ECG model, 0.559 for the clinical reference model, and 0.690 for the combined model; bootstrap confidence intervals for both AUC differences versus the clinical reference included zero. CONCLUSION: Shorter QRS duration and a more leftward frontal-plane QRS axis were associated with AL after esophagectomy. These QRS measurements are potential perioperative signals that require prospective validation rather than established predictors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Durvalumab consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is standard for unresectable, locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, long-term outcomes, treatment discontinuation impact, and the prognostic significance of immune-related adverse events (irAEs)-controlling for immortal time bias-remain unclear. We evaluated overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) by completion status and irAE occurrence in an exploratory single-center cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 59 consecutive NSCLC patients receiving durvalumab post-CRT (median follow-up: 53.6 months). Completion was defined as 12 months of therapy (completers, n=25; non-completers, n=34). Survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Time-dependent Cox regression evaluated irAE onset to adjust for immortal time bias, with sensitivity analyses stratified by discontinuation reason. Event-free patients were censored at last follow-up. RESULTS: Of 59 patients (median age: 70 years), 25 (42%) completed therapy, while 34 (58%) discontinued early (disease progression: n=16, adverse events: n=15, preference: n=3). During follow-up, 28 deaths [completers: 8/25 (32%); non-completers: 20/34 (59%)] and 36 progression events [completers: 9/25 (36%); non-completers: 27/34 (79%)] occurred. Completers achieved superior median OS (70.9 vs. 39.2 months; 5-year OS: 61% vs. 22%; P<0.01) and PFS (not reached vs. 7.9 months; 5-year PFS: 52% vs. 11%; P<0.001). Among non-completers (n=34, 20 deaths), time-dependent Cox analysis showed irAE onset reduced mortality risk [hazard ratio (HR) =0.384; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.147-0.999; P=0.0498], yielding a higher 5-year OS rate (43% vs. 0%, P=0.03). Stratified sensitivity analysis indicated a consistent directional trend, though limited by event counts (HR =0.44; 95% CI: 0.11-1.72; P=0.24). CONCLUSIONS: One-year durvalumab completion remains the primary clinical objective. In patients discontinuing early, irAE onset was associated with a potential prognostic signal after controlling for time-varying bias; however, these findings represent cautious, hypothesis-generating observations requiring prospective multi-center validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), has substantially improved clinical outcomes in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Nevertheless, acquired resistance inevitably develops, leading to disease progression in the majority of patients. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that anlotinib, a multi-targeted anti-angiogenic TKI, may overcome osimertinib resistance. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of continued osimertinib in combination with anlotinib in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who developed gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy. METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable stage III or IV EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who received first-line osimertinib therapy at The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China between January 2021 and December 2024. Eligible patients developed gradual progression after first-line osimertinib therapy. Subsequently, patients received combination therapy with osimertinib (80 mg orally once daily) plus anlotinib (10 mg orally on days 1-14 of every 3-week cycle). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included PFS rates at 6 and 12 months, objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS), OS rates at 12 and 24 months, and safety profile. RESULTS: A total of 52 patients were enrolled. The median age was 66 years. 40(76.9%) had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 0-1, 16 (30.8%) presented with brain metastases, 23 (44.2%) harbored exon 19 deletions, and 29 (55.8%) had L858R mutations. Molecular testing was performed in 12 patients after gradual progression. As of September 6, 2025, the median follow-up was 34.8 months, 48 PFS events were recorded and 22 patients died. The ORR was 7.7% (4/52), and the DCR was 86.5% (45/52). The median PFS (mPFS) was 9.9 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-12.1], with PFS rates of 61.5% at 6 months and 40.4% at 12 months. The median OS was not reached. OS rates were 86.3% at 12 months and 62.4% at 24 months. The exploratory multivariate COX analysis revealed that ECOG PS [hazard ratio (HR): 3.115, 95% CI: 1.111-7.706, P<0.001] and brain metastasis (HR: 2.242, 95% CI: 1.341-7.842, P=0.009) were associated with mPFS. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 9.6% (5/52) of patients. The most frequently observed AEs were diarrhea (42.3%, 22/52), hypertension (34.6%, 18/52), proteinuria (30.8%, 16/52), decreased appetite (28.8%, 15/52), and weight loss (28.8%, 15/52). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort focusing on the specific pattern of gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy, continued osimertinib combined with anlotinib demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity, which warrants further evaluation in prospective comparative studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are being evaluated in advanced small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the available trials include different targets, constructs, doses, and treatment settings. We aimed to determine the overall range of reported activity and safety while clarifying whether the evidence supports a clinically uniform ADC class effect. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), clinical-trial registries, and major oncology conference proceedings were searched from inception through July 31, 2026. Eligibility was restricted to reports with sufficient methodological and outcome information available in English; study country, recruitment region, investigator nationality, and participant ethnicity were not exclusion criteria. Prospective phase I-III studies of ADC monotherapy in adults with advanced, extensive-stage, relapsed, or refractory SCLC were eligible; no comparator was required, and only the ADC arm of comparative trials contributed to the single-arm synthesis. Outcomes were objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and clinically important safety events. Randomized trials were assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool and non-comparative studies using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). Random-effects models were used, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen prospective studies comprising 20 analytic cohorts and 2,246 patients were included: 12 phase I/Ib/I-II studies, three phase II studies, and three phase III studies. The pooled ORR was 34.38% [95% confidence interval (CI): 24.96-44.43%; I2=95.3%], and the pooled DCR was 77.50% (95% CI: 67.98-85.81%; I2=94.7%). The pooled median DOR, PFS, and OS were 4.99 months (95% CI: 4.24-5.86; I2=77.2%), 4.36 months (95% CI: 3.87-4.92; I2=84.8%), and 7.48 months (95% CI: 6.15-9.10; I2=92.6%), respectively. Subgroup analyses by intervention and target indicated substantial clinical and statistical heterogeneity. Safety was summarized by individual agent, dose, and source population because adverse-event definitions and denominators were not sufficiently comparable; the predominant hematologic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, and neurologic signals varied among products. Cochrane risk-of-bias judgments were predominantly low risk, with selected domains rated unclear or high risk. MINORS scores ranged from 11 to 15 of 16, with recurrent limitations in consecutive enrollment, blinded endpoint assessment, follow-up reporting, and prospective sample-size calculation. CONCLUSIONS: ADC-based therapy shows antitumor activity in advanced SCLC, but substantial clinical and pharmacological heterogeneity limits the interpretation of pooled single-arm estimates. Agent-specific randomized trials with standardized efficacy, safety, and biomarker reporting are needed.

papers.abstract_en: Verrucous carcinoma of the esophagus (VCE) is a rare type of esophageal cancer with a propensity for slow local spread. Early-stage cases are often treated with endoscopic resection. VCEs that extend beyond the submucosa are usually treated with esophagectomy if resection is feasible, and definitive chemoradiotherapy is frequently reserved for cases where patient or tumor factors contraindicate resection. There have been three reported cases of a complete pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for patients with VCE undergoing esophagectomy, but an approach to chemoradiotherapy for organ-preservation in operable patients has not been described. We describe a patient with an operable cT3N0M0 VCE managed with organ-preserving chemoradiation who achieved a complete clinical response, despite early discontinuation of his treatment. His clinical response was supported by serial bite-on-bite biopsies and post-treatment imaging. We review the outcomes of chemoradiotherapy for this rare disease and highlight the challenges of response assessment and surveillance that organ preservation entails.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The role of adjuvant ensartinib in patients with stage I ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with high-risk pathological features remains unclear. This multicenter retrospective study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjuvant ensartinib in this population. METHODS: A total of 393 patients with completely resected stage I ALK-positive NSCLC were included from five centers in China between March 2017 and March 2026. Patients were categorized into the ensartinib group (n = 63) and the observation group (n = 330). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were employed to balance baseline characteristics. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and safety. RESULTS: After IPTW, baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. The ensartinib group showed a higher 3-year DFS rate compared with the observation group (100% vs. 90.2%;P = 0.014). In patients with high-risk pathological features (micropapillary or solid subtypes or complex glandular pathological subtypes ≥10%, mucinous adenocarcinoma, or spread through air spaces), the 3-year DFS was 100% in the ensartinib group versus 86.5% in the observation group (P = 0.016). No significant difference in OS was observed between groups. Adverse events occurred in 87.3% of patients in the ensartinib group, all of which were grade 1-2, with rash being the most common adverse event (85.7%). CONCLUSION: Exploratory analyses suggested an association between adjuvant ensartinib and favorable DFS outcomes in stage I ALK-positive NSCLC patients exhibiting high-risk pathological features. A favorable safety profile was also observed. For patients without high-risk factors, the benefit of adjuvant ensartinib remains to be further clarified. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further prospective evaluation of risk-adapted adjuvant ALK-TKI therapy in stage I ALK-positive NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the association between resection extent and recurrence-free survival in patients with clinically node-negative NSCLC ≤3 cm with adverse pathologic features including visceral pleural invasion, spread through air spaces (STAS), or high-grade histology. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent curative-intent resection for cN0M0 NSCLC with pathologic tumor size ≤3 cm between 2017 and 2023. Patients were categorized into sublobar resection and lobectomy groups. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with recurrence-free survival. Propensity-score weighting was used to account for measured differences between the surgical groups, followed by weighted survival analyses within prespecified individual and combined adverse-feature subgroups. RESULTS: Among 1,774 patients, 666 underwent sublobar resection and 1,108 underwent lobectomy. Visceral pleural invasion, STAS, and high-grade histology were independently associated with a higher risk of recurrence. Lobectomy was not independently associated with recurrence-free survival in multivariable analysis (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 0.69-1.98, p = 0.562). In unadjusted subgroup analyses, recurrence-free survival did not significantly differ by resection extent among patients with visceral pleural invasion, STAS, or high-grade histology with similar findings in combined subgroups (p > 0.05). Weighting reduced the baseline imbalances, while the resulting survival curves remained largely overlapping across the individual adverse-feature subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: Visceral pleural invasion, STAS, and high-grade histology were independently associated with recurrence, whereas resection extent was not. The weighted analysis did not show a clear separation between surgical groups, although the present analysis was not designed to demonstrate comparable efficacy between the two surgical approaches.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (U-VATS) has gained widespread acceptance for anatomical pulmonary resection. However, concerns remain regarding its safety when performed by surgeons at an early stage of their surgical career. Evidence linking surgeon-related factors to perioperative outcomes remains limited. We examined the association between board certification status and perioperative outcomes using a nationwide multicenter U-VATS registry in Japan. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study used a nationwide U-VATS registry involving 43 institutions. Patients with primary lung cancer who underwent U-VATS lobectomy or segmentectomy between April 2018 and March 2023 were included. The primary outcome was surgical procedure-related complications. Propensity score matching and mixed-effects logistic regression with institutional random effects were applied. RESULTS: A total of 3532 patients were included, yielding 357 matched pairs. Surgical procedure-related complications occurred in 14.6% of the non-board-certified group and 11.2% of the board-certified group, with no statistically significant difference (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.86-2.19; p = 0.183). No statistically significant differences were observed in conversion to thoracotomy, additional port placement, operative time, readmission, or mortality between the groups. Postoperative drainage duration and hospital stay were shorter in the non-board-certified group. CONCLUSIONS: Board certification status was not associated with surgical procedure-related complications after U-VATS. These findings may support the implementation of U-VATS by non-board-certified surgeons within structured training systems and with appropriate intraoperative support.
