papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: The prognostic significance of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) completeness-of-resection classification after neoadjuvant therapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains poorly defined, particularly in the chemoimmunotherapy era. We evaluated its prognostic value in a contemporary real-world cohort. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection after neoadjuvant therapy for NSCLC between January 2017 and June 2026. Resections were retrospectively classified according to IASLC criteria as complete, uncertain, or incomplete. The primary endpoint was progression free survival (PFS) and the secondary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 98 patients, 45 (45.9%) had complete, 44 (44.9%) uncertain, and 9 (9.2%) incomplete resection; 51% received neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. After a median follow-up of 20.5 months, PFS decreased stepwise from complete to uncertain and incomplete resection (log-rank p = 0.07). After adjustment, incomplete resection was associated with an approximately threefold higher hazard of progression or death compared with complete resection, although statistical significance was not reached (HR 2.82, 95% CI 0.94-8.43; p = 0.064). Uncertain resection was not associated with PFS, and completeness-of-resection status was not independently associated with OS. CONCLUSIONS: IASLC completeness-of-resection status showed a clinically relevant PFS gradient after neoadjuvant therapy, with the poorest outcomes after incomplete resection. Although the adjusted association did not reach statistical significance, these findings support the clinical relevance and standardized reporting of the IASLC framework as a measure of oncological surgical quality in contemporary multimodal practice, including among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: First-line chemoimmunotherapy (CT-IT) is the standard treatment for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), while consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (cTRT) may improve local control and survival. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of cTRT after first-line CT-IT in patients with ES-SCLC in a real-world setting. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 199 patients with ES-SCLC who received first-line CT-IT. Patients were divided into a CT-IT + cTRT group (n = 97) and a CT-IT alone group (n = 102). Survival outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Treatment-related adverse events were assessed. RESULTS: The two groups were generally comparable at baseline, although the CT-IT + cTRT group had fewer brain metastases and more favorable response-related features after induction treatment. Median PFS and OS were significantly longer in the CT-IT + cTRT group (both P < 0.001). cTRT (P < 0.001) and a longer duration of maintenance immunotherapy (P = 0.031) were independently associated with a better PFS. For OS, cTRT was associated with better survival status (P = 0.003) and liver metastasis with poorer survival status (P = 0.015). Regarding safety, grade 1-2 dermatitis and gastrointestinal toxicity were more frequent in the CT-IT + cTRT group, whereas rates of pneumonitis, esophagitis, immune-related adverse events, and grade 3-4 toxicities were comparable between groups. CONCLUSION: In this real-world retrospective cohort, the addition of cTRT to first-line CT-IT was associated with significantly improved PFS and OS in patients with ES-SCLC, without an apparent increase in severe treatment-related toxicity. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and refine patient selection for cTRT.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Although the third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) Osimertinib is widely used in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), acquired resistance to this agent remains a major clinical challenge perplexing the academic community. While the genomic drivers of osimertinib resistance (OR) have been relatively well characterized, the non-genetic contributions of the tumor microenvironment (TME), especially the role of macrophage-mediated remodeling remains incompletely understood. METHODS: To address this gap, a total of 6 lung cancer tissue samples were collected from a cohort of 6 NSCLC patients and subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed on Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) data to screen out OR-associated gene modules. The intersection of scRNA-seq-derived differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and module genes was used to identify M2 macrophage- and OR-related DEGs (MORGs). An ensemble machine learning framework encompassing 112 algorithm combinations was applied to construct a gene signature. Survival analysis was conducted in the EGFR-mutant TCGA cohort. In vitro cell experiments were further performed for functional validation. RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing firstly revealed an increased proportion of M2 macrophages in the OR group, and M2 macrophage-specific DEGs were identified between OR and non-OR groups. A total of seven MORGs were obtained by intersecting DEGs and OR-related module genes. A 7-gene signature was successfully established via machine learning. Survival analysis demonstrated that RRBP1 showed the strongest association with overall survival and was selected for further investigation. In vitro experiments confirmed that RRBP1 was significantly upregulated in the H1975OR cells. Knockdown of RRBP1 reduced cell viability and migration, lowered the IC50 of osimertinib, and increased the expression of ER stress markers such as GRP78 and CHOP. CONCLUSION: In summary, our study identified a 7-MORGs signature for OR, among which RRBP1 may be a candidate regulator for OR.

papers.abstract_en: To evaluate real-world survival outcomes of consolidation immunotherapy after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) in patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated at a tertiary cancer center in Lebanon. This is a retrospective cohort study that included patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC treated between 2019 and 2025 with definitive cCRT, with or without ICIs (durvalumab or atezolizumab). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression methods, adjusting for variables, including PD-L1 status. Among 92 eligible patients, 52 (56.5%) received consolidation immunotherapy, and 40 (43.5%) received cCRT alone. Median follow-up was 22.3 months. Median PFS was 19.0 months (95% CI: 12.8-25.2) with ICIs versus 10.0 months (95% CI: 7.0-13.1) without (log-rank P=0.210). On multivariable Cox analysis, immunotherapy was associated with a favorable trend toward improved PFS (HR=0.53, 95% CI: 0.26-1.11; P=0.09). PD-L1 positivity independently predicted longer PFS (HR=0.42, 95% CI: 0.21-0.84; P=0.014), while high tumor grade predicted inferior outcomes (HR=1.89, 95% CI: 1.04-3.43; P=0.038). Immunotherapy after cCRT was associated with numerically and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS, consistent with the landmark PACIFIC trial. PD-L1 expression emerged as an independent prognostic and predictive biomarker, supporting biomarker-driven treatment strategies. These findings validate the clinical benefit of ICIs in a Middle Eastern low- and middle-income setting, reinforcing the importance of equitable access to immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The transformed small-cell lung cancer (T-SCLC) has a dismal prognosis, yet there remains a lack of standardized therapeutic guidelines. While this transformation is predominantly driven by concurrent loss of TP53 and RB1, retaining wild-type RB1 is exceptionally rare. We report a rare case of RB1-wildtype T-SCLC with prolonged survival to highlight its diagnostic challenges, potential biological mechanisms, and therapeutic management. CASE DESCRIPTION: A 57-year-old non-smoking woman with no significant prior medical history presented with persistent dizziness, headaches, and vomiting. She was diagnosed with EGFR-mutant stage IV lung adenocarcinoma (LADC; EGFR L858R/R776H, PIK3CA E542K, TP53 C176F; RB1 wild-type) following surgical resection of brain metastases. Primary lung biopsy was not feasible due to deep tumor location and marked vascularity. She received sequential dacomitinib [progression-free survival (PFS): 14 months] and osimertinib (PFS: 9 months), monitored by serial imaging and dynamic serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE). Rising NSE prompted re-biopsy of a liver metastasis, confirming small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) transformation at 35 months. She then received serplulimab, anlotinib, etoposide, and carboplatin; significant tumor regression was observed after two cycles, though grade 3-4 hematologic toxicities after the third cycle resolved with supportive care. Liver progression after six cycles prompted second-line nab-paclitaxel plus serplulimab and anlotinib, achieving renewed disease control for over 3 months. Treatment adherence was generally good throughout the clinical course. Overall survival (OS) was 5 years and 4 months, with post-transformation survival of 14 months. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights a rare RB1-wildtype transformation from EGFR-mutant LADC to SCLC, suggesting a distinct mechanism of lineage plasticity. Dynamic NSE elevation may serve as an early clinical indicator of transformation when tissue re-biopsy is challenging. The durable response achieved with serplulimab-based chemoimmunotherapy combined with anlotinib provides preliminary support for immunotherapy-based strategies in selected patients with T-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchopleural fistula (BPF) is a serious complication following lung resection, often leading to respiratory failure. In one study of 6,239 patients, 43 (0.65%) developed early BPF, and cases complicated by contralateral pneumonia have rarely been reported. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of a 74-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and pneumonia who developed BPF after thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy. The patient was scheduled to undergo BPF repair, in which includes an intercostal muscle flap was sutured in place. Due to extensive pneumonia and poor contralateral lung function, one-lung ventilation (OLV) along with high-flow veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-V ECMO) was used intraoperatively to maintain oxygenation. ECMO was managed without continuous systemic heparinization to reduce the risk of bleeding and to allow for postoperative epidural anesthesia (EA). The patient was extubated postoperatively under spontaneous breathing with adequate analgesia, avoiding tachypnea due to pain. Although the patient's initial postoperative course was uneventful, he experienced sudden massive hemoptysis on postoperative day 6 and died. CONCLUSIONS: Although this approach may be technically feasible in carefully selected cases, it should be considered a high-risk strategy for perioperative management during BPF repair in patients with severe lung injury. Given the limited evidence currently available, further data are needed to establish its safety and efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have significantly improved outcomes in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) but may induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including hypophysitis. Although endocrine irAEs usually present with nonspecific constitutional symptoms, atypical manifestations may delay diagnosis and expose patients to unnecessary invasive procedures. We report the case of a 76-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line nivolumab, ipilimumab, carboplatin, and pemetrexed who developed profound asthenia, altered mental status, bilious vomiting, and severe gastrointestinal dilation suggestive of acute mechanical bowel obstruction after two treatment cycles. Computed tomography demonstrated marked gastric and intestinal distension, and surgical management was initially considered. Endocrine evaluation subsequently revealed central hypothyroidism and secondary adrenal insufficiency, consistent with ICI-induced hypophysitis. Prompt initiation of physiological hormone replacement with intravenous hydrocortisone followed by thyroid hormone supplementation resulted in rapid neurological and systemic recovery, complete restoration of gastrointestinal motility, radiological resolution of bowel dilatation, and avoidance of surgery. Follow-up imaging also demonstrated a partial tumor response, which has remained durable for more than two years without additional anticancer treatment while the patient continues long-term endocrine replacement therapy. This case expands the clinical spectrum of ICI-induced hypophysitis by describing an unusual presentation as acute paralytic ileus mimicking mechanical bowel obstruction. It underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for endocrine irAEs in patients receiving ICIs who develop unexplained multisystem deterioration or apparent surgical abdomen. Early hormonal assessment and timely replacement therapy can be lifesaving, prevent unnecessary surgical interventions, and allow optimal multidisciplinary management without compromising oncologic outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. While epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as osimertinib (OS) and afatinib (AF), have markedly improved clinical outcomes, their efficacy is significantly hindered by the development of acquired resistance. Emerging evidence suggests that p38γ is involved in the progression of NSCLC and the emergence of resistance to EGFR-TKIs. However, whether the p38γ inhibitor pirfenidone (PFD) can enhance the sensitivity of NSCLC to EGFR-TKIs remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the synergistic antitumor effects of PFD in combination with OS or AF and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: EGFR-mutant NSCLC cell lines (PC9 and HCC827) and their OS-resistant derivatives (HCC827 OR) were utilized to evaluate cell proliferation by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays and colony formation experiments. Western blotting was performed to analyze the expression of p38γ, proteins within the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) signaling pathway, and autophagy-related markers. Drug interactions were assessed using the SynergyFinder platform. Autophagic flux was investigated via a dual-fluorescent adenovirus (mRFP-GFP-LC3) and further validated using the autophagy inhibitor bafilomycin A1. Additionally, an HCC827 nude mouse xenograft model was employed for in vivo validation. RESULTS: The combination of PFD with either OS or AF exhibited significant synergistic antitumor effects in both in vitro and in vivo NSCLC models, consistently achieving Bliss synergy scores exceeding 14. Notably, this combination successfully restored drug sensitivity in OS-resistant cells and reversed acquired resistance to EGFR-TKIs. Mechanistic investigations revealed that PFD enhanced EGFR-TKI sensitivity via two distinct pathways: firstly, by specifically inhibiting p38γ, a critical mediator of resistance, which leads to the downregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway; and secondly, by promoting the autophagy cascade in a p38γ-independent manner. These synergistic effects were not reversed by ferroptosis or pyroptosis inhibitors and were only partially attributed to apoptosis. CONCLUSIONS: PFD enhances the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs through a dual mechanism: first, by specifically inhibiting the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and second, by activating a p38γ-independent autophagy pathway. The activation of the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway may represent a key mechanism underlying OS resistance. This study provides the first evidence that PFD can restore drug sensitivity in OS-resistant cells, offering valuable experimental support for its potential clinical application as an EGFR-TKI sensitizer and a therapeutic strategy to overcome resistance in targeted cancer therapies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Gastric signet ring cell carcinoma (SRCC) typically metastasizes to the liver and peritoneum. Although pulmonary metastasis occurs in approximately 15% of patients with advanced gastric cancer and typically presents as multiple well-circumscribed nodules on chest computed tomography (CT), diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGOs) as the predominant manifestation of SRCC lung metastasis are exceedingly rare. This pattern may pose a diagnostic pitfall by closely mimicking infectious or interstitial lung diseases. CASE DESCRIPTION: We report two cases of gastric SRCC with pulmonary metastasis presenting primarily with respiratory symptoms and atypical imaging features. Case 1: A 64-year-old woman presented with persistent cough, dyspnea, and chest pain, and denied any preceding gastrointestinal symptoms. Chest CT revealed bilateral diffuse GGOs accompanied by pleural effusion and thickening. Despite empirical antibiotic therapy directed against Streptococcus pyogenes and Klebsiella pneumoniae identified by next-generation sequencing, her symptoms worsened. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) demonstrated intense metabolic activity [maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) 6.2] in the lung lesions and bilateral pleural involvement. Bronchoscopy-guided biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma with signet ring cell features, and gastroscopy with biopsy of a depressed gastric angle lesion confirmed poorly differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma. She received docetaxel plus oxaliplatin chemotherapy with symptomatic improvement and was discharged. Case 2: A 62-year-old woman presented with exertional dyspnea and intermittent cough, also without preceding gastrointestinal symptoms. CT imaging demonstrated right pleural effusion, pleural thickening, and ground-glass nodules. Empirical antibiotic therapy was ineffective. Pleural fluid analysis revealed elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA; 85.00 µg/mL) and cancer antigen 125 (CA125; 327.00 U/mL). Biopsy of an adnexal mass and gastric lesions confirmed gastric SRCC with pleural and ovarian metastases. She was referred to the oncology department for systemic therapy. Long-term follow-up data for both patients are not available in the medical records. CONCLUSIONS: These cases highlight an atypical imaging pattern of gastric SRCC metastasis-diffuse GGOs with pleural involvement-that closely mimics benign lung diseases. In patients without known malignancy who present with unexplained respiratory symptoms, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusion or thickening, and poor response to anti-infective therapy, early lung or pleural biopsy is essential to prevent diagnostic delay and initiate timely systemic oncological treatment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastasis remains an important clinical concern in patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC), even after prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI). Accurate identification of patients at high risk of brain metastasis after PCI may facilitate individualized surveillance and management. This study developed a fusion model based on two-and-a-half-dimensional (2.5D) multi-channel deep learning features, clinical features, and radiomics features to predict whether patients with SCLC will develop brain metastases following PCI. METHODS: This retrospective study included 185 patients with SCLC who underwent PCI and randomly divided them into a training set (N=148) and a testing set (N=37). A 2.5D multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) model was constructed based on multi-planar regions of interest (ROI) derived from CT images to extract 2.5D deep learning features. Based on the largest cross-section and three-dimensional (3D) volume of the tumor ROI, two-dimensional (2D) and 3D deep learning features were extracted, respectively. Subsequently, features from different dimensions were fused with clinical features and traditional omics features to construct the 2D_clinic_Rad, 2.5D_clinic_Rad, and 3D_clinic_Rad models, respectively. The performance differences between the 3D models and the clinical and traditional radiomics models were then compared. RESULTS: The 2.5D_clinic_Rad fusion model demonstrated the best performance in predicting brain metastases, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.841 on the test set, outperforming clinical models, traditional radiomics models, and 2D and 3D deep learning fusion models. Analysis of decision curves and calibration curves indicated that the 2.5D_clinic_Rad model demonstrated the highest clinical net benefit and the best calibration consistency compared to other models. CONCLUSIONS: The fusion model based on 2.5D_clinic_Rad can effectively predict the risk of brain metastasis in patients with SCLC following whole-brain prophylactic irradiation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly from a surgery-centered approach toward biomarker-informed, multimodality care integrating staging, pathology, surgery, perioperative systemic treatment, and postoperative surveillance. In Vietnam, implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions, particularly in access to fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), invasive mediastinal staging, molecular testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. This project aimed to develop a Vietnamese multidisciplinary expert consensus to contextualize contemporary international evidence for clinical practice in Vietnam. METHODS: A structured, modified Delphi-informed consensus process was conducted in Vietnam between August 2025 and January 2026. The workflow comprised seven stages: scoping; a baseline practice survey; initial draft development; expert review of parts 1 and 2; post-meeting written feedback, revision, electronic recirculation, and formal voting for these sections; a multidisciplinary consensus meeting and formal voting for parts 3 and 4; and editorial harmonization and consolidation. The panel included specialists in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, respiratory medicine, pathology, nuclear medicine, radiation oncology, and related disciplines. Classes of recommendation were adapted from the European Society of Cardiology framework. All statements submitted to formal consensus voting were formally rated, with consensus predefined as at least 75% agreement. RESULTS: The final document comprised 35 consensus statements across four domains: preoperative diagnosis and staging (n=7), surgery and postoperative surveillance (n=8), neoadjuvant and perioperative treatment (n=12), and adjuvant treatment (n=8). Across the meeting rosters, 32 unique experts were identified, with strong representation from thoracic surgery and medical oncology. The baseline survey and expert discussions highlighted implementation gaps in FDG-PET/CT, invasive mediastinal staging, biomarker testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. All 35 consensus statements met the predefined threshold, with agreement ranging from 82% to 100%. CONCLUSIONS: These consensus statements provide a multidisciplinary, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis and management of resectable NSCLC across the perioperative pathway. By contextualizing international evidence within Vietnamese clinical practice, the document may help improve consistency of care, support biomarker-guided and multimodality treatment, and strengthen multidisciplinary decision-making across institutions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab is a standard first-line treatment for advanced or recurrent non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable driver alterations, including tumors with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score (TPS) <50%. However, the clinical benefits vary, and biomarkers for this chemoimmunotherapy regimen remain limited. CBM588, a live biotherapeutic preparation containing Clostridium butyricum MIYAIRI, may modulate antitumor immunity by affecting the gut microbiota. The MIYABRO study aims to evaluate the additive efficacy and safety of CBM588 with platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab and to explore longitudinal gut microbiota dynamics. METHODS: This is a multi-institutional, single-arm, phase II exploratory study enrolling 20 treatment-naïve patients with advanced or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC and a PD-L1 TPS <50%. Patients will receive continuous CBM588 from the start of the protocol treatment in combination with platinum, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab. After four induction cycles, maintenance pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab will be continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoints are response rate and progression-free survival (PFS). Tumor response will be assessed according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Stool samples will be collected before treatment, cycle 3, and cycle 5 for 16S rRNA sequencing to evaluate microbial diversity and responder-associated taxa. DISCUSSION: This trial will prospectively assess CBM588 added to platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab in NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS <50% while monitoring the gut microbiota. These findings may inform microbiota-targeted strategies for optimizing chemoimmunotherapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (No. jRCT1071260004) on 6 April 2026.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), nevertheless, the inevitable occurrence of osimertinib resistance after a long-term administration limits its clinical application in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Xanthatin, a naturally active component from Xanthium Strumarium L., has been shown to possess multiple bioactive effects. However, whether xanthatin can ameliorate osimertinib resistance remains unclear. PURPOSE: The present study aimed to clarify the role and detailed mechanism of xanthatin in reversing osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. METHODS: Combenefit analysis, LDH release assay, and EdU staining were employed to evaluate the effect of xanthatin on osimertinib cytotoxicity in osimertinib-resistant (OR) NSCLC cells. Quantitative proteomics combined with bioinformatics and network pharmacology analysis was used to uncover the specific target of xanthatin. Xanthatin-triggered HMGCR protein degradation was assessed by bio-layer interferometry, drug affinity responsive target stability assay, cycloheximide chase assay and ubiquitination determination. The function of xanthatin on cholesterol homeostasis was measured via the detection of HMGCR activity, total cholesterol, triglycerides and lipid droplets as well as MDR1 distribution in the lipid rafts. The function of MDR1 was examined via a rhodamine 123 efflux assay. The accumulation and efflux of osimertinib were monitored using FITC-labeled osimertinib. The effect of HMGCR on the cytotoxicity of xanthatin was evaluated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments in HMGCR-overexpressing NSCLC OR cells. RESULTS: Xanthatin restored the sensitivity of NSCLC OR cells to osimertinib, accompanied by the induction of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Proteomic data indicate that oxidative stress and metabolic reprogramming contribute to xanthatin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC OR cells. Through further integration with network pharmacology, we identified HMGCR (a key enzyme of cholesterol metabolism) as a potential target of xanthatin. We confirmed xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR protein (KD=6.753 μM), subsequently facilitating AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGCR. Xanthatin diminished intracellular cholesterol biosynthesis and MDR1 levels in lipid rafts. HMGCR overexpression mitigated the cytotoxicity of xanthatin and sustained cholesterol homeostasis, enabling tolerance to the combined effects of xanthatin and osimertinib. Conversely, HMGCR-deficient NSCLC OR cells were more vulnerable to osimertinib. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates for the first time that xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR and promotes AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination of HMGCR, which in turn accelerates HMGCR degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, leading to reduced cholesterol synthesis, less distribution of MDR1 in lipid rafts, ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial dysfunction-associated apoptosis, ultimately restoring osimertinib sensitivity in NSCLC cells. Therefore, xanthatin may represent a preclinical natural product candidate for the reversal of osimertinib resistance in NSCLC cells, which requires further translational verification in future studies.

papers.abstract_en: EGFRC797S mutation and bypass pathway activation are major drivers of acquired resistance to osimertinib; however, no approved therapeutic agents are currently available to effectively overcome this resistance. In this study, a series of aminopyrimidine-based small-molecule inhibitors were rationally designed and synthesized. The lead compound 6a exhibits potent single-digit nanomolar activity against EGFRL858R/T790M/C797S (IC50 = 1.76 nM), along with equipotent ALK inhibitory activity (IC50 = 1.95 nM) that may address ALK-mediated bypass resistance. In cellular assays, 6a potently inhibits proliferation of osimertinib-resistant H1975-M3 cells (IC50 = 0.035 μM), suppresses downstream oncogenic signaling, induces G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, and impairs cell migration and invasion. In vivo, 6a demonstrates robust antitumor efficacy in an H1975-M3 xenograft model with a tumor growth inhibition rate of 86.47% at 30 mg/kg, significantly outperforming brigatinib (55.53%), while exhibiting favorable safety and pharmacokinetic profiles. Collectively, these findings establish 6a as a promising therapeutic candidate for overcoming osimertinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer is one of the most striking examples of the success of multimodal treatment concepts in gastrointestinal oncology. For locally advanced, resectable adenocarcinoma, perioperative chemotherapy with the FLOT regimen has replaced neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy according to CROSS following the ESOPEC trial and represents the current standard, whereas for squamous cell carcinoma neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery remains established. Immunotherapy is expanding the treatment spectrum: adjuvant nivolumab is established for residual disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CheckMate-577); perioperative durvalumab combined with FLOT improves event-free survival in gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer (MATTERHORN). The SANO trial demonstrated noninferiority of active surveillance versus standard esophagectomy with respect to 2‑year overall survival in clinical complete responders; however, a decision analytical model based on the SANO data published in 2026 suggests potential long-term advantages of standard resection. In oligometastatic disease, FLOT5/RENAISSANCE showed no overall survival benefit for supplementary surgical resection and in this situation patient selection remains the central challenge. Future strategies will concentrate more on biological criteria, with a more precise definition of oligometastatic constellations, integrated immunotherapy and emerging biomarkers such as circulating tumor DNA.

This case was a locally advanced hypopharyngeal cancer patient who received neoadjuvant immunotherapy and total laryngectomy with partial hypopharyngectomy. During follow-up, a mass was found in the middle part of the trachea, protruding into the tracheal lumen. The peculiarity of this case was that the tracheal mass was located in the middle part of the trachea, with a narrow lumen. During anesthesia, whether the tracheal intubation was placed above or below the mass would affect the operation. After multidisciplinary team discussion, a no-intubation anesthesia plan was adopted, using esketamine, which could maintain spontaneous breathing well, ensure sufficient depth of anesthesia, and reduce the occurrence of bronchospasm. The airway management mainly used high-flow nasal cannula to provide a large flow and flow rate, prolonging the safe period without breathing and oxygenation, providing a safety guarantee for the operation and ensuring its successful completion.

papers.abstract_en: Low-dose computed tomography screening has markedly increased the detection of small, deeply located subsolid pulmonary nodules, and local therapy for these lesions now encompasses anatomical segmentectomy, tailored sublobar resection, lobectomy, and image-guided thermal ablation. Although multidisciplinary pathways already inform modality selection, three-dimensional (3D) anatomical reconstruction - despite its established role in segmentectomy planning - is rarely used as a shared patient-specific dataset to guide both resection and ablation decisions. In this perspective, a thoracic surgeon argues that, for a deep or cross-segment subsolid nodule with an established indication for local therapy, a single patient-specific 3D dataset can inform both branches of the decision. The same volumetric anatomy - including nodule size and consolidation-to-tumor ratio, segmental boundaries, bronchovascular relationships, pleura, and the chest wall - is first used to determine whether adequate-margin lung-sparing resection is achievable and, if it is not, to assess whether ablation is anatomically feasible through three sequential filters: trajectory safety, perilesional structural risk, and predicted ablative coverage. The approach is illustrated with a representative case and discussed in the contexts of multifocal disease, the post-resection lung, and perivascular lesions, together with the trade-offs associated with forgoing nodal staging and tissue diagnosis. The framework does not expand indications beyond those already supported by guidelines. Rather, it operationalizes these recommendations through patient-specific anatomy, with the aim of making modality selection more transparent, reproducible, and auditable. It remains an unvalidated, single-center proposal that requires prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: AIM: This study aimed to systematically review machine learning (ML) methods applied to computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)/CT for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and for lung cancer histological subtype classification. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to May 31, 2026. Eligible studies applied ML, deep learning, or radiomics to CT, PET, or PET/CT for primary versus metastatic lung lesion differentiation or major lung cancer histological subtype classification. Methodological quality was assessed with Quality assessment of comparative diagnostic accuracy studies (QUADAS-2), and reporting was evaluated using 10 prespecified Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging-aligned items. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included after eligibility reassessment. Twenty-one provided a numeric study-level Area Under the Curve (AUC); the median representative AUC was 0.889 (IQR 0.820-0.936). The median AUC was 0.923 for primary/metastatic differentiation and 0.874 for histological subtype classification. Only 5 of 22 studies (22.7%) used independent external testing; among 4 externally validated studies with numeric AUCs, the median was 0.720. QUADAS-2 showed frequent uncertainty in patient selection (17/22, 77.3%), while CLAIM-aligned assessment identified limited external testing, code/model availability (3/22, 13.6%), and explainability reporting (4/22, 18.2%). CONCLUSION: CT- and PET/CT-based ML models show promising diagnostic performance for lung lesion-origin and histological subtype classification, but performance is lower in independent external evaluation. Broader multicentre validation, transparent reporting, reproducible code/model access, and prospective assessment are required before routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Bevacizumab (Bev) improves the response and survival rates in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This phase II trial aimed to assess the feasibility of adding Bev to preoperative chemotherapy in resectable non-squamous NSCLC. METHODS: Patients with clinical stage II/IIIA non-squamous NSCLC (n = 30) received three cycles of cisplatin (Cis), pemetrexed (Pem), and Bev, followed by surgical resection. The primary endpoint was the complete resection rate (CRR), defined as the proportion of all eligible enrolled patients who ultimately underwent complete (R0) resection. The sample size was set at 30 patients. Treatment was considered feasible if the CRR exceeded the predefined acceptable threshold of 65%. RESULTS: Radiological tumour reduction was observed in 29 of 30 patients (97%). Twenty-eight patients (93%) completed all three cycles of chemotherapy, and 25 patients (83%) underwent surgery. Five patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events (n = 3), disease progression (n = 1), or patient refusal (n = 1). Complete resection was achieved in all resected patients, yielding an 83% CRR (two-sided 80% confidence interval, 71.3%-91.7%). The objective response rate was 37%, and pathological complete response of the primary tumour was achieved in 3 patients (12%). Grade 3 toxicities included neutropenia (7%), nausea (7%), hypertension (23%), and pulmonary embolism (3%). No grade 4/5 adverse events occurred within 28 days, and no treatment-related deaths occurred within 84 days. CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative Cis, Pem, and Bev for clinical stage II/IIIA non-squamous NSCLC met the predefined feasibility criterion, with acceptable safety in this selected population. These findings provide historical insights supporting perioperative anti-vascular endothelial growth factor-based systemic intensification.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Thoracoscopic resection of pulmonary metastases offers a minimally-invasive approach but requires preoperative localization due to absent tactile feedback. CT-guided methylene blue staining (MBS) was implemented to facilitate resection of pulmonary metastases, including intermediate-to-deep lesions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed pediatric patients (0-18 years) undergoing resection of pulmonary metastases (2007-2024). Lesion depth was classified as superficial (≤ 10 mm), intermediate (11-20 mm), or deep (> 20 mm). Primary endpoint was completeness of resection; secondary endpoints included perioperative and oncological outcomes. Subgroup analysis included patients with ≤ 2 pulmonary metastases. RESULTS: Fifty-eight resections in 43 patients were included: 49 open, and 9 thoracoscopic following CT-guided MBS. Eleven lesions were stained prior to thoracoscopic resection: three superficial, seven intermediate, one deep lesion. All were resected with negative margins, without complications. Thoracoscopy following CT-guided MBS was associated with shorter operative times (65 vs. 157 min, p = 0.01), hospital stay (4.0 vs. 5.6 days, p = 0.01), and time-to-chemotherapy-resumption (2.25 vs. 18.6 days, p = 0.01). No differences were observed in pulmonary recurrence, disease-free interval, or six-month-survival. CONCLUSION: In pediatric patients with up to two pulmonary metastases, CT-guided methylene blue staining provided feasible preoperative localization, facilitating thoracoscopic wedge resection of superficial, intermediate and deep lesions without complications. Prospective multicenter studies should further evaluate efficacy and inclusion criteria.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are designed to deliver cytotoxic agents directly to tumor cells by conjugating an antigen-specific monoclonal antibody with a potent payload. By recognizing tumor-associated antigens and undergoing intracellular processing, ADCs enhance antitumor activity while minimizing damage to normal tissues. This review focuses on the research progress of ADCs targeting non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), providing an in-depth analysis of their mechanisms of action, molecular design, and clinical efficacy, with particular emphasis on novel ADCs targeting HER2, TROP2, and DLL3. Despite challenges such as target specificity and drug resistance, clinical trial data demonstrate that ADCs exhibit significant therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of both NSCLC and SCLC. The article also discusses emerging strategies to overcome current limitations, including innovative linker technologies, development of bispecific ADCs, and exploration of combination treatment plans. Given that lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, ADCs technology holds promise for delivering breakthrough advances in improving therapeutic outcomes and alleviating the societal burden of the disease. With ongoing research into ADCs, future clinical applications may provide more precise and effective treatment options for patients with lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis. The baseline YOLOv8 model, although efficient, is prone to missed detections due to non-maximum suppression (NMS)‑induced suppression of small nodules and insufficient feature extraction for morphologically complex lesions. To address these clinical challenges, this study aimed to optimize YOLOv8 by integrating a real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) decoder head and an aggregated attention mechanism, thereby improving detection sensitivity and accuracy for PNs of varying sizes and shapes. METHODS: The proposed model, termed YOLOv8‑RTA, integrates an RT‑DETR‑based transformer decoder head into YOLOv8, replacing the original detection head to mitigate NMS‑induced suppression of true boxes, and introduces an aggregated attention mechanism within the backbone to expand the effective receptive field and enhance deep feature discriminability. Training and evaluation were performed on the Tianchi dataset, with five‑fold cross‑validation and an external test on 50 hospital Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) computed tomography (CT) scans. RESULTS: YOLOv8‑RTA achieved precision of 93.28%, recall of 92.4%, and mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP50) of 94.98% on the Tianchi dataset. Compared to the baseline YOLOv8 model, which achieved an mAP50 of 90.6%, the proposed method improved the detection accuracy by 4.38 percentage points. It also outperformed RT‑DETR‑R18, which attained an mAP50 of 93.51%, by a margin of 1.47 percentage points. The model contains only 6.24 million parameters and runs at 12.2 giga floating point operations per second (GFLOPs). In five‑fold cross‑validation, the mAP50 ranged from 75.4% to 99.3%, with a mean value of 91.5%. On the external PACS dataset, the model detected all 50 nodules, achieving a mean confidence score of 0.86 for nodules smaller than 5 mm. CONCLUSIONS: This study proposes YOLOv8‑RTA, a collaborative hybrid network that combines an RT‑DETR decoder head and an aggregated attention module to enhance multi‑scale feature extraction and discriminative representation for PN detection. On the Tianchi dataset, the model achieved improved performance over baseline YOLOv8 and RT‑DETR‑R18, with gains of 4.38 and 1.47 percentage points in mAP50, respectively, while maintaining a lightweight architecture of only 6.24 million parameters. A preliminary test on 50 real‑world PACS CT images suggests potential clinical feasibility, with all nodules successfully detected in this limited cohort. These findings indicate that YOLOv8‑RTA offers a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade‑off for PN screening. Future work will focus on larger multi‑center validation, patient‑level cross‑validation, and extension to three-dimensional (3D) context modelling.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary nodules are frequently identified on thoracic CT imaging, with management guided by established clinical pathways. Thoracic CT scans are reported by both specialist and general radiologists. This study evaluated discordance in pulmonary nodule identification and management between general and specialist radiologists and modeled automated triage to a virtual nodule clinic (VNC). METHODS: All CT scans, including the thorax, performed over a 1-week period at a single UK center in March 2022 were identified and original reports reviewed. Oncology follow-up scans were excluded. Reports were categorized and compared with an independent second expert radiologist review. VNC triage pathways were modeled to select patients for second review by an expert radiologist. The pathways used combinations of original radiologist reports and automated nodule assessment (DeepHealth Ltd) to trigger VNC review. The cost implications of each pathway were calculated. RESULTS: Among 243 CT scans, 98 (40%) original reports identified a pulmonary nodule. Expert review identified incorrect recommendations in 24/243 (10%) cases. Errors were significantly more frequent in reports issued by general radiologists compared with specialist thoracic radiologists (χ² ∼ 11.0, df = 2, P < .05). VNC triage pathways that selected cases for secondary review when automated nodule assessment failed to identify a nodule that was identified by the reporting radiologist resulted in the greatest cost savings per corrected nodule. CONCLUSION: Approximately 10% of thoracic CT scans contained errors in pulmonary nodule reporting. Cost-saving triage pathways combining non-specialist reporting with automated nodule assessment appear feasible and warrant prospective real-world validation. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study demonstrates theoretical clinical implementation of semi-automated triage to a virtual nodule clinic and provides an evidence base for prospective study.

No conversion to alternative approaches or perioperative mortality occurred in either group. CONCLUSIONS: SURT using the da Vinci Xi system provides a favorable midline surgical view, minimal invasiveness through a uniportal approach, and excellent operability through a robotic system. This procedure can be performed safely with careful port positioning at the subxiphoid incision site.

papers.abstract_en: Minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) has evolved significantly over the past two decades, shifting from conventional median sternotomy toward sternal-sparing approaches that offer reduced surgical trauma, lower complication rates, and faster patient recovery. As incision size has progressively decreased, the field has advanced toward totally endoscopic cardiac surgery (TECS), in which the entire intracardiac procedure is performed exclusively under thoracoscopic visualization. Despite growing adoption, the transition from direct-vision MICS to TECS remains technically demanding and operationally complex. Drawing on our institutional experience at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, and a review of the current literature, we provide a comprehensive overview of the key elements required to successfully build and sustain a TECS program. These include a working definition of totally endoscopic surgery, a proposed four-phase surgeon training pathway, simulation-based learning strategies, robotic credentialing, team-based training, technical instrumentation, scope management, patient selection criteria, procedural challenges, and postoperative outcomes. Both non-robotic and robotic-assisted endoscopic platforms are discussed. Large-scale evidence confirms that MICS and TECS achieve outcomes equivalent or superior to sternotomy, with low mortality and stroke rates, and significantly improved health-related quality of life. Notably, non-robotic TECS offers a scalable and cost-effective pathway that does not require an expert bedside assistant, can address multiple pathologies simultaneously, and is feasible across diverse healthcare settings. Emerging technologies-including articulated robotic instruments, artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging, and next-generation robotic platforms-are expected to further expand the reach and safety of fully endoscopic cardiac procedures.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) followed by durvalumab consolidation is the current standard of care for unresectable locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC). However, survival outcomes in this setting remain unsatisfactory. Although the PACIFIC trial improved outcomes, further intensification of systemic therapy may be required to improve long-term survival. Preclinical and perioperative clinical evidence suggests that introducing immunotherapy in the presence of an intact primary tumor may enhance antitumor immune responses. Recently, early-phase studies have reported the feasibility and potential efficacy of induction chemo-immunotherapy followed by cCRT; however, its clinical benefit has not been confirmed in a phase III trial. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, phase III trial is designed to determine whether the addition of induction chemo-immunotherapy to the current standard strategy of cCRT followed by durvalumab consolidation improves survival outcomes in patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC. Previously untreated patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC without activating EGFR mutations are randomized 1:1 to receive either cCRT followed by durvalumab consolidation or induction chemo-immunotherapy followed by cCRT and durvalumab consolidation. Randomization is adjusted for age, clinical stage, programmed death-ligand 1 expression, and institution. The primary endpoints are progression-free and overall survival. Secondary endpoints include objective response rate, proportion of patients proceeding to cCRT after induction therapy, and adverse events. A total of 212 patients will be enrolled from 60 institutions over 5 years. CONCLUSION: The results of this trial should clarify whether the addition of induction chemo-immunotherapy can enhance curative potential and lead to improved overall survival in patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC.

HALS was performed in 202 patients and laparoscopy in 60 patients. Surgical procedures and perioperative outcomes were compared between the groups. RESULTS: Blood loss and total operative time did not differ significantly between the groups, although the transhiatal procedure tended to require a longer operative time with laparoscopy (p = 0.09). The approach used for middle mediastinal lymphadenectomy was similar between the two groups (43% vs. 35%, p = 0.28), and the overall number of dissected lymph nodes, excluding the upper mediastinal and cervical nodes, was comparable. However, significantly more abdominal lymph nodes were dissected with laparoscopy than with HALS (17.9 vs. 15.7, p = 0.04). Laparoscopic gastric mobilization and lymph node dissection were safely performed, with no significant differences in the rate of postoperative complications or curability. CONCLUSIONS: The totally laparoscopic transhiatal technique is a feasible and safe approach for mediastinoscopic esophagectomy, with surgical outcomes comparable to those of HALS and not inferior abdominal lymph node dissection. It may be particularly advantageous for cases requiring meticulous abdominal lymphadenectomy.

papers.abstract_en: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical access and one-lung ventilation (OLV) may generate distinct systemic and local inflammatory responses after lung resection. We compared perioperative cytokine profiles in serum, pleural fluid, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open thoracotomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: This prospective, single-center, non-randomized observational study included 40 adults undergoing anatomical lobectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection (VATS, n = 20; open thoracotomy, n = 20). Surgical access was selected according to patient preference. TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 were measured in serial serum and pleural-fluid samples and in BAL from both lungs before OLV and after resection. Results: Serum and pleural-fluid cytokines peaked at 4 h in both groups. Exploratory pointwise comparisons showed that at 24 h, serum TNF-α (4.89 [IQR, 4.43-5.92] vs. 4.01 [IQR, 3.75-5.12] pg/mL; p = 0.010), IL-6 (150.22 [IQR, 136.90-194.66] vs. 108.00 [IQR, 100.46-125.88] pg/mL; p < 0.001), and IL-8 (66.83 [IQR, 57.70-82.82] vs. 43.62 [IQR, 32.89-50.59] pg/mL; p = 0.001) were higher after thoracotomy than after VATS; differences at 48 h persisted for TNF-α (2.48 [IQR, 1.86-3.04] vs. 1.99 [IQR, 1.19-2.23] pg/mL; p = 0.010) and IL-8 (16.92 [IQR, 15.09-23.99] vs. 7.42 [IQR, 6.44-11.30] pg/mL; p < 0.001). Pleural-fluid IL-6 at 24 h and IL-8 at 48 h were also higher after thoracotomy, whereas BAL cytokines did not differ significantly by approach. Longitudinal GEE analyses showed significant approach-by-time interactions for serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 and for pleural-fluid IL-8, but not for pleural-fluid IL-6. Conclusions: VATS was associated with a lower systemic proinflammatory response than open thoracotomy, while differences in the pleural compartment were more limited and no detectable difference was observed in early alveolar cytokine responses. These findings highlight compartment-specific differences in perioperative inflammatory responses between VATS and open thoracotomy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying doses of aerosolized Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) on oxygenation and intrapulmonary shunt fraction (Qs/Qt) during One-Lung Ventilation (OLV) under 60% Fraction of Inspired Oxygen (FiO2). Secondary objectives included evaluating the impact on intraoperative hypoxemia, postoperative Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs). DESIGN: A prospective, single center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial. SETTING: The study was conducted at a single academic medical center. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 160 patients aged 65‒84 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III and Body Mass Index (BMI) < 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective esophageal cancer surgery were enrolled. Patients with certain comorbidities, respiratory diseases, or contraindications to PGE1 were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Group L ‒ Received 0.1 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group M ‒ Received 0.2 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group H ‒ Received 0.3 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group C (control) ‒ Received normal saline nebulization. Nebulization was performed for 10-minutes via a modified breathing circuit into the ventilated lung before initiating OLV. MEASUREMENTS: Arterial blood gas parameters (arterial partial pressure of oxygen, PaO2; arterial oxygen saturation, SaO2; arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide, PaCO2), hemodynamic variables (Mean Arterial Pressure [MAP]; Heart Rate [HR]), respiratory mechanics (Peak airway pressure [Ppeak]; dynamic lung compliance [Cdyn]), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and Qs/Qt were recorded at multiple time points during OLV. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia and hypotension, PPCs within 7-days, and CPIS on postoperative day-2 were also assessed. MAIN RESULTS: All PGE1 groups showed significantly improved PaO2, SaO2, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and reduced Qs/Qt during the first 30-minutes of OLV compared to the control group. The High-dose group (H) demonstrated the greatest improvement in oxygenation. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [Group L: 0/40 (0%), Group M: 0/40 (0%), Group H: 0/40 (0%), Group C: 3/40 (7.5%)] and hypotension did not differ significantly among groups; however, the hypoxemia finding was exploratory as the study was not powered for this endpoint. No significant differences were observed in PPCs incidence among groups, but group H was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 compared to group C. Hemodynamic changes were transient and clinically manageable. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulized PGE1 at doses of 0.1-0.3 μg/kg improves oxygenation and reduces Qs/Qt during OLV under 60% oxygen, with the 0.3 μg/kg dose being most effective. It did not significantly reduce the incidence of PPCs within 7-days. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was lower in the PGE1 groups (0/120) compared with the control group (3/40), but this was an exploratory finding as the study was not powered for this endpoint. The higher dose (0.3 μg/kg) was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 (3.3 vs. 4.1), but CPIS is a surrogate marker, and this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. The clinical significance of this small difference is uncertain, as changes of this magnitude are below the typically recognized thresholds for meaningful clinical improvement. Hemodynamic monitoring is recommended when using higher doses of PGE1.

papers.abstract_en: Trilaciclib, a cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor administered before chemotherapy, reduces chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), but its efficacy across solid tumors remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of trilaciclib in solid tumor patients receiving chemotherapy. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to January 21, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing chemotherapy with or without trilaciclib were included. Primary outcomes were severe neutropenia (SN), febrile neutropenia (FN), duration of severe neutropenia (DSN), Grade 3/4 leukopenia, and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) use. Secondary outcomes included other hematologic toxicities, supportive care interventions, and efficacy outcomes. Ten studies involving 1172 patients (six RCTs and four cohort studies) were identified. Trilaciclib significantly reduced SN (OR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.06-0.31; p < 0.001), FN (OR, 0.19; 95% CI, 0.11-0.36; p < 0.001), Grade 3/4 leukopenia (OR, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.13-0.46; p < 0.001), and G-CSF use (OR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.18-0.71; p = 0.0087), and shortened DSN (MD, -2.30 days; 95% CI, -4.28 to -0.31; p = 0.0309). It also reduced Grade 3/4 anemia and thrombocytopenia and decreased use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, red blood cell transfusions, and platelet transfusions. Overall survival showed a borderline improvement (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.71-0.99; p = 0.0373), while no significant differences were observed in progression-free survival, overall response rate, or non-hematologic adverse events. Subgroup analyses suggested greater benefit in ES-SCLC. Overall, trilaciclib before chemotherapy significantly reduced CIM and supportive care needs, with no apparent compromise in antitumor efficacy and more pronounced effects in ES-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) remains a potentially life-threatening adverse event that may be mitigated through structured pharmaceutical care interventions. OBJECTIVE: To assess the effectiveness of pharmacy services in reducing the occurrence of CIP among patients with NSCLC receiving ICIs. METHODS: Patients who underwent immunotherapy at our hospital between November, 2023 to September, 2024 were selected and randomized into the control and intervention groups (105 patients each). Intervention group received 6 months of pharmacy services, and CIP occurrence, clinical efficacy, medication adherence, and quality of life at 3, 6, and 9 months were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a significantly lower CIP incidence and immunotherapy suspension rate due to CIP (2.9% vs. 9.5%, P = 0.043), as well as significantly improved medication adherence at all time points (P < 0.05). The intervention group also had lower CIP severity and longer onset time (8.6 months vs. 6.2 months), along with numerically higher ORR (40.6% vs. 30.3%) and DCR (81.2% vs. 71.7%), and a favorable trend in emotional function scores; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacy care can reduce the incidence and severity, and increase the onset time of CIP, thus enhancing drug safety.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Esophageal leiomyoma is the most common benign mesenchymal tumor of the esophagus. Minimally invasive management is performed by thoracoscopic surgery or endoscopic resection, but comparative evidence remains limited. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes and treatment-selection patterns for thoracic and endoscopic resection. METHODS: Patients with pathologically confirmed leiomyoma who underwent resection between January 2015 and September 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with malignant components, biopsy/fine-needle aspiration only, or incomplete data were excluded. A 1:1 propensity score matching analysis was performed using nearest-neighbor matching with a caliper of 0.1, matching age, sex, tumor location, and maximal tumor diameter. RESULTS: A total of 1,348 patients were included in the primary analysis: 132 underwent minimally invasive thoracic surgery and 1,216 underwent endoscopic resection. In the endoscopic group, 54.5% underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection and 45.5% underwent submucosal tunneling endoscopic resection. In the MIS group, 62 patients (47.0%) received intraoperative endoscopic assistance. Endoscopic resection was associated with shorter operative duration (41.9 ± 39.9 vs 114.8 ± 71.0 min, p < 0.001) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001), whereas minimally invasive thoracic surgery was used for larger tumors (median 5.0 vs 1.3 cm, p < 0.001). After matching, 113 pairs were analyzed. Endoscopic resection remained associated with shorter operative duration (73.7 ± 62.9 vs 111.6 ± 61.5 min, p = 0.009) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 3.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001). In the matched cohort, nasogastric tube placement and delayed stay of 5 days or longer were less common after endoscopic resection. CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic resection was associated with faster postoperative recovery in patients with esophageal leiomyoma, whereas thoracic surgery remained important for larger tumors and complex lesions. These findings support a size- and location-oriented treatment strategy rather than a universal preference for either approach.

papers.abstract_en: Objective: We sought to assess the outcomes of octogenarians compared to a reference group of younger patients undergoing robotic anatomic lung resection for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to better understand the postoperative expectations of this elderly patient population. Methods: A prospectively maintained Institutional General Thoracic Surgery Database was queried for patients aged 80 years and above (octogenarians) and 65-75 years (reference group) undergoing robotic lobectomy or segmentectomy for NSCLC between 2015 and 2026. Clinical data and postoperative outcomes were collected and compared using both unadjusted and 1:1 propensity-score matching. Results: In total, 822 patients were identified: 101 in the octogenarian group (mean age 82.4 years [standard deviation 2.2]) and 721 in the reference group (69.7 [3.1], p < 0.001). Postoperative complications that were more frequent in octogenarians included pneumothorax requiring chest tube insertion (5.9% vs. 2.2%, p = 0.043), atrial arrhythmias (18.8% vs. 9.2%, p = 0.005), and urinary tract infections (6.9% vs. 1.7%, p = 0.005). Air leak, atelectasis, pneumonia, respiratory failure, pleural effusion, empyema, and delirium did not differ between the groups. After propensity matching, there were no significant differences in the aforementioned postoperative outcomes. While the unadjusted length of stay was longer in octogenarians (4 days [interquartile range 3-5] vs. 3 [2-5], p = 0.012), this was no longer significant after matching (4 [3-5] vs. 3 [2-5], p = 0.369). There were no statistically significant differences in 30-day readmission rates (p = 0.197) or 30-day mortality (p = 0.781) after propensity-score matching. Conclusions: Among carefully selected octogenarians undergoing robotic anatomic lung resection for NSCLC, no statistically significant differences in short-term postoperative outcomes were detected compared with patients aged 65-75 years after adjustment for baseline differences. These findings support individualized surgical selection beyond chronologic age alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Identification of metastasis status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation. OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields. METHODS: Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data. RESULTS: More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F1-score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F1-score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F1-score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F1-score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F1-score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F1-score=0.79). CONCLUSIONS: All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Chemoradioimmunotherapy (CRIT) with 60-66 Gy is the standard of care (SoC) for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) UICC stage III. The aim of this real-world data (RWD) study was to report the long-term impact of Durvalumab and radiation dose escalation on clinical outcomes. MATERIAL AND METHODS: ALLSTAR is a nationwide prospective multicentre registry for NSCLC UICC stage III, in which 12/14 Austrian centres participated (ethics approval number: 1002/2019). The basis for the current analysis is the third data extraction, which was completed on 2 June 2025. Apart from the SoC, alternative dose-fractionation and sequential CRT concepts >66 Gy were also permitted. Durvalumab maintenance treatment for one year was administered at the discretion of the tumour board at each centre. RESULTS: Compared to prior analyses by our group, 40 individuals who completed follow-up (FUP) were added to this final analysis, leading to a total patient population of 228 (156 CRT plus Durvalumab; 72 CRT). In 156 patients, Durvalumab was added to CRT, while 72 received CRT only. The median FUP periods were 41.0 (95%-CI: 36.7-45.4) and 37.8 months (95%-CI: 31.4-44.1) for the Durvalumab and CRT cohort, respectively. Radiation dose escalation combined with Durvalumab treatment was associated with a nominally higher ITC of 37 months (95%-CI: 24.5-not reached) compared with 17.7 months (95%-CI: 14.9-not reached) in patients receiving neither dose escalation nor Durvalumab (N = 135; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.37-1.006; p-value 0.051). With Durvalumab maintenance, a median PFS of 22.8 months (95%-CI: 19.4-38.3) was observed compared to 16.5 months (95%-CI: 12.6-24.5) without (N = 228; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.88; p-value 0.0071). Median OS was 52.6 months (95%-CI: 39.5-not reached) with Durvalumab compared to 27.4 months (95%-CI: 18.7-not reached) without (N = 228; HR = 0.52; 95%-CI: 0.34-0.78; log-rank p-value < 0.002). Median time to death or distant metastasis (TTDM) was 33.3 months (95%-CI: 23.5-45) in the Durvalumab cohort compared to 18.7 months (95%-CI: 14.8-not reached) in the CRT cohort (N = 228; HR = 0.60; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.89; log-rank p-value 0.01). Median time to death or local relapse (TDLR) with Durvalumab was 30.4 months (95%-CI: 23.5-51.1) compared to 17.2 months (95%-CI: 14.8-25.7) without (N = 226; HR = 0.58; 95%-CI: 0.40-0.83; log-rank p-value < 0.003). CONCLUSION: This final RWD analysis implies both a beneficial effect of high-dose irradiation combined with Durvalumab on ITC and the long-lasting impact of Durvalumab on PFS, OS, TTDM, and TDLR.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have become a standard treatment option for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, considerable heterogeneity exists among patients regarding treatment response and survival. This study aimed to determine whether the pretreatment modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS), a marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, is prognostically associated with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated with nivolumab at a single tertiary oncology center. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 130 adult patients with histologically confirmed advanced/metastatic NSCLC who received nivolumab at the Department of Medical Oncology, Çukurova University Faculty of Medicine. The pretreatment mGPS (0, 1, or 2), derived from baseline serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin levels, was analyzed in relation to PFS and OS using the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression. The prognostic value of mGPS was tested in multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR); the proportional hazards assumption was formally tested, and the incremental discriminative contribution of mGPS was assessed using bootstrap resampling. Results: Among 130 patients, 83.8% received nivolumab as second-line therapy. Pretreatment mGPS was 0, 1, and 2 in 40 (30.8%), 55 (42.3%), and 35 (26.9%) patients, respectively. Median OS was not reached, 9.7 months, and 3.0 months across mGPS 0, 1, and 2, respectively; corresponding median PFS values were 10.2, 4.8, and 3.0 months (log-rank p < 0.001 for both endpoints). After adjustment for age, sex, ECOG performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and NLR, each one-point increase in mGPS remained associated with worse OS (adjusted HR 2.38; 95% CI 1.64-3.46; p < 0.001) and PFS (adjusted HR 1.81; 95% CI 1.32-2.48; p < 0.001), independent of the covariates included in the model. The proportional hazards assumption held for mGPS in both models. Addition of mGPS to the clinical-variables-only model was associated with higher model discrimination (Harrell's C-index: 0.676 to 0.737 for OS and 0.620 to 0.666 for PFS), a difference confirmed as statistically significant by bootstrap resampling (2000 iterations; 95% CI for the difference excluding zero, p < 0.001 for both endpoints). Conclusions: Pretreatment mGPS is a simple, readily available marker that shows a robust prognostic-rather than treatment-predictive-association with both OS and PFS in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated predominantly as second-line nivolumab monotherapy. Its addition to established clinical variables was associated with a statistically significant, though modest, improvement in prognostic discrimination. These findings require prospective, multicenter validation, including in first-line immunotherapy settings, before mGPS can be recommended for routine clinical risk stratification.
