papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: The CRP-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index is promoted both as a marker of postoperative morbidity and as a prognostic factor for survival. These claims are rarely tested together, thresholds usually come from the dataset in which they are then tested, and the index is seldom compared against its components. We examined both in one minimally invasive esophagectomy cohort. Methods: Consecutive esophagectomies with a thoracoscopic or robotic thoracic phase at one centre were reviewed. The index was derived from the preoperative albumin, C-reactive protein, and lymphocyte count. Short-term endpoints were major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ 3) and anastomotic leak; survival was analysed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods, with internal cut-points stress-tested by bootstrapping. Results: Of 154 esophagectomies screened, 22 open or transhiatal procedures and one exploration without resection were excluded, leaving 131 patients. Major morbidity occurred in 39 (29.8%), and leak in 21 (16.0%). The index discriminated neither: area under the curve 0.556 (95% CI: 0.450-0.663) and 0.481 (95% CI: 0.339-0.623). Over a median follow-up of 31.0 months, there were 39 deaths, and median survival was 62.1 months. Here, the index behaved differently: each unit of log-CALLY carried a hazard ratio of 0.776 (95% CI: 0.643-0.936, p = 0.008), and three-year survival rose from 48.5% in the lowest tertile to 77.1% in the highest (trend p = 0.020). The association held after adjustment for stage and nodal status (0.749, 95% CI: 0.609-0.922, p = 0.006), lifting the concordance index of a stage-based model from 0.699 to 0.741. However, entered with CRP, the index lost significance. Conclusions: The index said nothing useful about early surgical morbidity yet was independently associated with survival, although that signal did not survive adjustment for CRP alone. It belongs with prognostic markers rather than perioperative risk scores.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical resection remains an important treatment option for selected patients with bronchiectasis who have persistent symptoms, recurrent pulmonary infections, or hemoptysis despite medical therapy. This study evaluated perioperative and follow-up outcomes after pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis in a predominantly video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)-treated cohort. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients who underwent pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis between January 2009 and January 2026. Baseline and follow-up data were analyzed at the patient level, whereas operative and perioperative outcomes were assessed at the procedure level. Follow-up duration was calculated from the most recent resection to the last available clinical assessment. Results: Thirty-four patients underwent 37 pulmonary resections. Multilobar disease was present in 14 procedures (37.8%). VATS was used in 30 procedures (81.1%) and thoracotomy in 7 (18.9%). Median hospital stay was 11 days (range, 4-41). Postoperative complications occurred after 6 procedures (16.2%), with no 30-day mortality. Complete or partial symptomatic improvement occurred after 31 procedures (83.8%). Median follow-up was 20.8 months (interquartile range, 5.9-58.8; range, 0.4-144.2). At the last available clinical assessment, 23 patients (67.6%) had no recorded symptoms; recurrent hemoptysis occurred in 1 (2.9%) and recurrent pulmonary infection in 2 (5.9%). Conclusions: Pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis was associated with acceptable morbidity, no 30-day mortality, and a high rate of postoperative clinical improvement in this VATS-dominant cohort. Most patients had no recorded symptoms at their last available clinical assessment, while recurrent hemoptysis and pulmonary infection were uncommon.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The necessity of routine pulmonary parenchymal wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations (CLMs) in children remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association of routine wound closure with drainage-related recovery, perioperative outcomes, one-year computed tomography (CT)-based lung re-expansion, and the procedural learning curve. METHODS: Consecutive children who underwent thoracoscopic sublobar resection for CLMs between January 2021 and March 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The cohort was divided into a non-closure group and a routine-closure group according to wound management strategy. Pulmonary wound closure was performed using an absorbable barbed suture, generally proceeding from the peripheral or lower-tension side toward the central or higher-tension region. Irregular wounds were managed by initiating closure from multiple peripheral points converging centrally while preserving the natural axis of residual bronchi and vasculature. Outcomes included chest tube duration, drainage volume, prolonged air leak, chest tube reinsertion, postoperative hospital stay, perioperative complications, one-year CT-based volumetric indices, and closure-time learning curve metrics. RESULTS: A total of 285 children were included, comprising 75 in the non-closure group and 210 in the closure group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-closure group, the closure group exhibited significantly shorter chest tube duration (0.87 ± 0.74 vs. 2.81 ± 1.99 days, P < 0.001), lower postoperative drainage volume (2.12 ± 0.70 vs. 7.21 ± 2.58 mL/kg/day, P < 0.001), reduced rates of prolonged air leak and drainage failure, and shorter postoperative hospital stay (5.63 ± 0.83 vs. 7.68 ± 2.10 days, P < 0.001). At one-year follow-up, CT-based volumetric assessment revealed no evidence that wound closure restricted residual lung re-expansion. Closure time decreased from approximately 22 min in the early phase to 11 min in the late phase, with learning curve inflection points identified at cases 47 and 135. CONCLUSIONS: Routine pulmonary wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for pediatric CLMs was associated with improved drainage-related recovery and shorter hospitalization, without compromising one-year lung re-expansion on CT. Although closure adds a procedural step, efficiency improved substantially with experience, demonstrating a quantifiable learning curve.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Therapeutic strategies after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) remain suboptimal in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We investigated whether continuing EGFR inhibition with lazertinib combined with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy could extend clinical benefit after progression on prior lazertinib. METHODS: In the multicenter, single-arm, phase II LUCAS study (NCT05786430), patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who had progressed on lazertinib received lazertinib 240 mg daily plus pemetrexed-carboplatin for four cycles, followed by maintenance lazertinib and pemetrexed. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, safety, and exploratory ctDNA analyses. RESULTS: Of 86 patients, 46.5% had a history of brain metastases. Among 81 response-evaluable patients, median PFS was 9.5 months (95% CI: 6.3-9.6; one-sided p = 0.017 against a null median of 6.0 months). In the safety population, median OS was 15.9 months (95% CI: 12.4-20.0) and ORR was 36.0% (95% CI: 26.0-47.1). Outcomes were similar irrespective of prior lazertinib line or EGFR subtype. Baseline ctDNA-detected EGFR amplification was associated with inferior survival. Among 36 patients with radiologically evident baseline brain metastases, median intracranial PFS was 9.9 months (95% CI: 7.8-16.4) with infrequent isolated intracranial progression. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events occurred in 69.8%, predominantly hematologic, without new safety signals. CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of lazertinib with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy after progression on prior lazertinib was associated with meaningful systemic and intracranial activity and manageable toxicity. Randomized evaluation is required to establish the incremental benefit of lazertinib continuation.

papers.abstract_en: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (NIVATS) minimises airway trauma and ventilator-induced lung injury, yet its application in complex, multi-phase McKeown oesophagectomy is seldom reported. A 32-year-old female (40 kg, 140 cm and body mass index: 20.4 kg/m 2 ) presented for McKeown minimally invasive oesophagectomy following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. We employed a 'less invasive anaesthesia' strategy combining T9-T10 thoracic epidural analgesia with Bispectral Index-guided target-controlled propofol infusion. Continuous pressure support ventilation (16 cmH 2 O above a positive end-expiratory pressure of 5 cmH 2 O) with preserved spontaneous breathing was maintained via a size 3 i-gel™ throughout surgery; neuromuscular blockade and controlled mechanical ventilation were not used at any stage. Surgical exposure was optimised via right-sided capnothorax. The resulting permissive hypercapnia was haemodynamically well-tolerated. Recovery was uneventful, and the airway device was removed after protective airway reflexes had returned. She was discharged from the hospital on post-operative day 6 without any complications. NIVATS for McKeown oesophagectomy may be feasible in carefully selected patients.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. RESULTS: Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. CONCLUSIONS: Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet predicting durable benefit and detecting resistance remain major challenges. As immunotherapy expands across disease stages, minimally invasive tools are increasingly needed to monitor response and inform treatment personalization. Liquid biopsy enables serial assessment of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and other blood-based biomarkers, complementing tissue analysis and imaging. This review critically synthesizes evidence across resectable, locally advanced, and metastatic NSCLC, integrating ctDNA dynamics with emerging multi-omics approaches. Its contribution is to distinguish the prognostic value of circulating biomarkers from evidence that using them to guide treatment improves patient outcomes, while identifying priorities for clinical translation. Across the reviewed studies, ctDNA clearance is associated with favorable outcomes, whereas persistent or rising ctDNA signals an increased risk of recurrence or progression, sometimes before radiological detection. Methylation, fragmentomics, plasma proteomics, and immune-cell profiling may provide complementary information on tumor-immune interactions. However, low tumor shedding, clonal hematopoiesis, assay variability, and unvalidated intervention thresholds limit routine use. The expansion of perioperative immunotherapy and emerging interest in biomarker-guided treatment adaptation make this synthesis timely. Prospective interventional trials are needed to determine whether liquid biopsy can safely guide treatment escalation, de-escalation, or discontinuation. By clarifying both the promise and the limitations of longitudinal monitoring, this review informs research aimed at detecting ineffective treatment earlier and reducing unnecessary treatment exposure while preserving cancer control.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Chronobiology may influence outcomes in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its prognostic role in early-stage disease remains unclear. We evaluated the association between perioperative chronobiological variables, systemic inflammation, and long-term outcomes after complete resection for stage I NSCLC. METHODS: 587 patients who underwent curative-intent resection for pathological stage I NSCLC between 2009 and 2018 were retrospectively reviewed. Chronobiological and inflammatory variables included season of surgery (spring/summer [21st March-22nd September], autumn/winter [23rd September-20th March]), time of day, day of week, and preoperative (CRP0 levels: low ≤ 3 mg/L, high > 3 mg/L) and postoperative day-3 (CRP3 levels: low ≤ 126 mg/L, high > 126 mg/L) C-reactive protein levels. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets to develop and validate a prognostic model for overall survival (OS), taking into consideration the follow-up time. Disease-free survival (DFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 6.7 years, with 80 deaths and 108 recurrences recorded. In the training set, older age (p = 0.0049), stage IB disease (p = 0.0301), high CRP0 (p = 0.0049), and high CRP3 (p = 0.0280) were associated with worse OS, while surgery performed during autumn/winter was associated with improved OS (p = 0.0312). The multivariate Cox model including age, stage, and season of surgery showed the best prognostic performance (C-index 0.67, 95% Bonferroni-adjusted CI 0.50-0.83) and was internally validated in the testing cohort (C-index 0.69, 95%CI 0.52-0.86). The resulting linear predictor remained associated with both OS and DFS in the overall population. CONCLUSIONS: A simple model integrating age, pathological stage, and season of surgery was associated with long-term outcomes after surgery in stage I NSCLC. This model provides an exploratory framework integrating host-, tumor-, and chronobiological dimensions of prognosis. These findings require external validation and further investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying seasonal variation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy defined by rapid progression, early metastasis, and profound therapeutic resistance. Its extensive heterogeneity across genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental levels continues to undermine precision medicine. Emerging evidence highlights the complex role of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to SCLC, and the influence of distinct transcriptional subtypes on clinical behavior. METHODS: This review synthesizes current literature encompassing nucleic-acid-based determinants of resistance, SCLC molecular architecture, transformation biology, and subtype evolution, integrating findings from genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, imaging, and clinical studies. We additionally evaluated artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies with potential to unify multi-omics, radiomics, and clinical variables to model subtype plasticity, clonal evolution, and therapy-induced rewiring. RESULTS: The evidence demonstrates that traditional single-layer analyses are insufficient to capture the multiscale architecture of SCLC biology or the nonlinear interactions driving resistance, whereas AI-enabled multi-omics approaches offer advantages in enhancing subtype classification, supporting early detection, and improving prediction of therapeutic response. Key barriers such as tissue scarcity, limited biomarker availability, and extreme intratumoral heterogeneity remain significant challenges, though increasingly addressable through integrative computational frameworks. CONCLUSION: AI-driven systems-level integration reframes SCLC as a dynamically evolving, multilayered disease process, where nucleic-acid alterations are central to subtype evolution and treatment resistance, providing a conceptual model to guide biomarker discovery and therapeutic development. By leveraging AI-enabled multi-omics and radiomics, this framework has the potential to advance personalized clinical management and overcome longstanding diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer (LC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, representing a major public health challenge. Although low-dose computed tomography is currently the standard screening method for high-risk individuals to reduce mortality, its clinical performance is limited by false-positive findings and restricted accessibility. Emerging biomarker-based liquid biopsy offers a promising non-invasive approach for cancer detection. This narrative review provides a critical overview and evaluation of clinically endorsed liquid biopsy applications for guiding treatment in advanced-stage lung cancer, as well as investigational advances in liquid biopsy for early cancer detection. We also address challenges of current liquid biopsy technologies, the integration of artificial intelligence, implementation improvements, and future perspectives for their adoption into routine clinical practice. To complement this narrative review, a structured search of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry was performed to identify clinical trials evaluating liquid biopsy in lung cancer. Current evidence supports the clinical use of liquid biopsy for molecular profiling and treatment selection in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), whereas its application in early detection, screening, and minimal residual disease (MRD)-guided management remains investigational and requires further prospective validation. Overall, liquid biopsy represents a promising complementary approach to advance precision oncology and improve lung cancer management.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives:MET amplification represents the most common bypass resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) treatment in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Combination therapy with the EGFR-TKI, osimertinib, and the MET-TKI, crizotinib, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in overcoming this resistance. However, assessing MET transcriptional activity during treatment remains challenging. Methods: Cell-free chromatin immunoprecipitation (cfChIP) targeting H3 lysine 36 trimethylation (H3K36me3) was employed to investigate the transcriptional activity of the EGFR and MET genes in serial liquid biopsies obtained from two patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to quantify circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cfChIP enrichment levels. Results: In PT1, H3K36me3 mEGFR and MET cfChIP enrichment increased during disease progression, with MET enrichment increasing further following the initiation of crizotinib/osimertinib combination therapy, during which the patient experienced a partial response. In PT2, MET amplification was detected in a liquid biopsy, but MET cfChIP enrichment remained low throughout the treatment course, and the patient did not respond to crizotinib. Conclusions: This two-patient feasibility study illustrates the potential of cfChIP-ddPCR for the longitudinal assessment of EGFR and MET transcriptional activity in liquid biopsies. These observations warrant further investigation of cfChIP as an approach for monitoring transcriptional activity during osimertinib/crizotinib treatment.

papers.abstract_en: The concept of personalized medicine has tremendous appeal-tailoring diagnosis and treatment to an individual, rather than a "one-size-fits-all" approach. The management of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has rapidly evolved toward strategies increasingly guided by tumor biology and precision oncology. The safety and significant efficacy of biomarker-directed therapies in metastatic disease have fueled interest in applying precision oncology to early-stage, operable NSCLC. Advances in molecular profiling have revealed that a substantial proportion of resected NSCLC harbor actionable driver mutations, enabling the integration of targeted therapies into the perioperative setting. The success of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor and anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibition established a framework for biomarker-driven therapy and highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing at diagnosis. In parallel, perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-based strategies have expanded treatment options for appropriately selected patients, further emphasizing the importance of molecular profiling. Significant implementation gaps remain, including incomplete molecular testing, delayed results, inadequate tissue sampling, fragmented workflows, and disparities in access. Beyond clinically actionable driver mutations, emerging research highlights radiogenomics and advances in the use of circulating tumor DNA for minimal residual disease detection, with important implications for early recurrence detection and patient prognostication, although these technologies differ in clinical maturity. Collectively, these developments emphasize the molecular heterogeneity underlying early-stage NSCLC and the expanding role of biomarkers in guiding clinical decision-making. Integrating genomic, radiographic, and biologic markers into clinical workflows will be essential to refine risk stratification, personalize perioperative treatment strategies, and ultimately improve long-term oncologic outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Esophageal cancer (EC) is an aggressive malignancy, and outcomes following esophagectomy are influenced by both oncological and perioperative factors. This study aimed to identify clinicopathological and perioperative factors associated with overall survival (OS) after esophagectomy for EC and, secondarily, to evaluate factors associated with 90-day mortality. Methods: A total of 101 patients who underwent radical esophagectomy with two-field lymphadenectomy between April 2016 and April 2023 were retrospectively evaluated. The primary outcome was OS, defined as the time from esophagectomy to death from any cause or the date of last follow-up. The secondary outcome was 90-day postoperative mortality. OS was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses, whereas 90-day mortality was assessed using Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression because of the limited number of events. Results: During follow-up, 74 patients (73.3%) died, including 11 deaths within 90 days after esophagectomy. The estimated 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS rates were 80.1%, 44.8%, and 38.0%, respectively. In the whole-cohort multivariable Cox model, stratified by surgical approach, lymph node positivity was associated with poorer OS (HR 10.57, 95% CI 4.78-23.38; p < 0.001). Among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (n = 76), lymph node positivity (HR 6.34, 95% CI 2.60-15.45; p < 0.001) and pathological non-response (HR 2.96, 95% CI 1.13-7.73; p = 0.027) were associated with poorer OS. In exploratory Firth regression analysis, lymph node positivity (OR 103.11, 95% CI 7.40 -> 1000; p < 0.001) and intraoperative complications (OR 75.58, 95% CI 7.42 -> 1000; p < 0.001) were strongly associated with 90-day mortality. Conclusions: Lymph node positivity was consistently associated with poorer OS both in the entire cohort and among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Pathological non-response was additionally associated with poorer OS in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy subgroup, while lymph node positivity and intraoperative complications were strongly associated with 90-day mortality.

papers.abstract_en: Clinical translation of T cell bispecific (TCB) therapies in solid tumors is hindered by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and intratumoral heterogeneity, features poorly captured by standard preclinical models. We applied an integrated translational framework, combining humanized mouse models, a patient-derived ex vivo organ culture (EVOC) platform, and Phase 1 clinical trial data (ClinTrials.gov identifier NCT03539484), to define the biologic determinants of functional reactivity to a CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB. In humanized mice bearing CEA-positive tumors, the TCB inhibited tumor growth and increased intratumoral T cell infiltration. EVOC, which preserves native 3D tumor architecture and endogenous tumor immune contexture, revealed rapid TCB-induced secretion of IFNγ, IL-2, TNFα, and IL-10 across colorectal, pancreatic, and non-small cell lung cancer patient tumors, with substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. Higher baseline CD3+ T cell infiltration trended with a greater magnitude of cytokine release in patient tumors treated with the TCB ex vivo versus tumors with lower CD3+ T cell infiltration. Baseline tumor CEA expression did not associate with functional response in EVOC. In the Phase 1 trial, on-treatment peripheral cytokine induction was greater in patients with immune-inflamed or -excluded tumors as compared to those with immune-desert tumors. EVOC recapitulated the high inter-patient functional heterogeneity observed clinically, with a coefficient of variation for IFNγ of 135% in EVOC versus 190% in patients, compared with 52% in humanized mice. These findings suggest that early pharmacodynamic responses to CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB associate with a pre-existing tumor immune state rather than target antigen expression alone and support integration of patient-derived ex vivo models for modeling clinically-relevant pharmacodynamics.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv (teliso-V) versus docetaxel in previously treated high c-Met protein-overexpressing (≥50% of tumor cells with 3+ staining) advanced nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer. METHODS: A partitioned survival model with monthly cycles and a five-year horizon was built from the US healthcare sector perspective. Individual time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves of the c-Met High subgroup (N=78) of LUMINOSITY and the CONTACT-01 docetaxel arm (N=180). Because individual covariate data were unavailable, a naive (unadjusted) indirect comparison was conducted. Seven parametric distributions were fit independently by arm; their median and range were the primary summary. The analysis was preregistered. RESULTS: The unadjusted overall survival hazard ratio favored teliso-V but was not statistically significant (HR 0.690; 95% CI 0.471-1.010). The median incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was approximately $2.0 million per QALY (range, $1.7-$2.2 million). Across 70,000 probabilistic iterations, cost-effectiveness was not achieved in any iteration at $50,000, $100,000, $150,000, or $200,000 per QALY. The threshold payment limit at $150,000 per QALY was approximately $1,209 per 100 mg (92% reduction). CONCLUSIONS: At the current Medicare Part B payment limit, telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv is unlikely to be cost-effective versus docetaxel in the US high c-Met protein-overexpressing population at conventional willingness-to-pay thresholds. The conclusion was robust to modeled survival extrapolation and parameter uncertainty. Because the comparison is unadjusted, comparative effectiveness remains uncertain pending randomized results.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive esophagectomy has become the preferred surgical approach for esophageal cancer, with uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) emerging as a potential refinement over conventional multiportal VATS (mVATS). However, comparative evidence remains limited to small single-centre studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate perioperative and safety outcomes of uVATS versus mVATS in patients undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and CNKI from inception through April 2026. Studies directly comparing uVATS with mVATS in adults undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy were eligible. Binary outcomes were pooled as odds ratios and continuous outcomes as mean differences under REML random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. RESULTS: Nine studies comparing uVATS and mVATS were included. uVATS was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain on day one (MD - 2.10, 95% CI - 3.63 to - 0.57; I² = 99.3%), reduced postoperative pneumonia (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.76; I² = 43.5%), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 2.13 days, 95% CI - 3.64 to - 0.63; I² = 96.8%). No significant differences were observed between approaches for anastomotic leakage (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.61-2.09), overall complications (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.47-1.32), recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.43-1.85), perioperative mortality (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.16-1.81), intraoperative blood loss, or total operative time. CONCLUSION: UVATS esophagectomy appears to be a feasible and safe alternative to mVATS, with potential advantages in postoperative pain, pulmonary morbidity, and hospital stay while maintaining comparable perioperative safety. The evidence base remains limited by high heterogeneity and predominance of observational studies. Multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term oncologic follow-up are needed to consolidate these findings.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis exhibit a unique immunological state characterized by chronic inflammation and T-cell dysfunction. Evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of combination chemoimmunotherapy in dialysis patients remains extremely limited. CASE REPORT: We report a case of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (performance status 1, cT1cN2M1c, stage IVB) in a patient undergoing maintenance hemodialysis who received 4 cycles of carboplatin (300 mg/m2, day 1), etoposide (50 mg/m2, days 1 and 3), and durvalumab (1,500 mg/body, day 1). Treatment was safely continued after adjusting the dosing schedule and dose levels in accordance with the dialysis schedule. Although new brain metastases developed during treatment and whole-brain radiotherapy was administered, computed tomography after 4 cycles demonstrated a partial response, and durvalumab maintenance therapy was subsequently continued. Grade 4 thrombocytopenia and grade 3 anemia and neutropenia were observed as adverse events; however, these were manageable with transfusion support and dose reduction. Disease progression was subsequently observed. CONCLUSION: Carboplatin, etoposide, and durvalumab can provide meaningful therapeutic benefit even in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis when adverse events are appropriately managed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multi-organ transplant recipients face a substantial long-term risk of infection, malignancy, and chronic rejection secondary to prolonged immunosuppression. Sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations remain rare, resulting in limited evidence to guide perioperative management and long-term follow-up. CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old man underwent sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations in 2012, 2018, and 2022, respectively. Initial graft function was favorable under an immunosuppressive regimen comprising tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids. From 2023 onwards, he developed recurrent SARS-CoV-2 infections, lung cancer requiring a segmentectomy, recurrent lower-extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans, and progressive renal allograft failure. He ultimately died from cardiopulmonary arrest precipitated by severe metabolic acidosis and electrolyte derangements complicating renal allograft failure. DISCUSSION: This case suggests that patients undergoing sequential multi-organ transplantations can achieve meaningful long-term survival with multidisciplinary care and individualized immunosuppression. Nevertheless, complications related to cumulative immunosuppression remain a major challenge, necessitating dynamic follow-up and tailored post-transplant management. CONCLUSION: Sequential liver, kidney, and heart transplantations are feasible in carefully selected patients. However, the delayed adverse effects of chronic immunosuppression pose a major threat to long-term outcomes, underscoring the absolute necessity for vigilant monitoring and highly individualized pharmacological management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Predicting patient response to immunochemotherapy is vital but challenging and poorly studied in the (neo)adjuvant setting. We showed that tumor monocyte content (TMC) predicts overall survival of advanced esophageal cancer (OC) in response to immunochemotherapy. We report clinical outcomes of 35 operable OC patients receiving ICI-based therapy and molecular profiling of the unique phase-2 LUD2015-005 trial treating 73 OC patients (38 advanced/inoperable and 35 operable) in the (neo)adjuvant setting. METHODS: LUD2015-005 trial patients were treated with 4-week immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-only before combination with standard of care. Paired and longitudinally collected biopsies of tumor and multiple adjacent normal sites were bi-dissected to extract DNA and RNA. Whole-genome, methylome, single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data generated from the entire LUD2015-005 cohort were used for cell-deconvolution and data integration analysis. FINDINGS: Neoadjuvant ICI-based combination therapy of operable OC in the LUD2015-005 trial revealed improved overall outcomes. Tumor monocytes contribute to tumor immune microenvironment (TiME) remodeling and associate with tumor reactive CD8+ T cells upon ICI+ chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy. We identified five DNA-methylation subtypes with distinct TiME and a TMC-related five-gene signature CFISH (CXCL8, FCN1, IFI30, SLC11A1, and HLA-DRA) as highly predictive biomarkers of overall survival in OC and beyond. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of the myeloid compartment in ICI response and the potential of CFISH and tumor DNA methylation in patient stratification for immunochemotherapy. papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant therapy has recently become an integral component of multimodal treatment for resectable lung cancer. However, real-world data on perioperative morbidity and treatment adherence remain limited. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of different neoadjuvant treatment approaches applied within daily clinical routine. We retrospectively analyzed patients with resectable stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer undergoing either neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy or chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy followed by curative surgical resection. Treatment groups were compared with respect to perioperative outcomes, radiologic and pathologic downstaging, and pathologic response. A total of 143 patients met the inclusion criteria, of whom 46 (32.2%) received chemoimmunotherapy and 97 (67.8%) were treated with chemotherapy prior to surgery. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in only two patients in the chemoimmunotherapy group and four patients in the chemotherapy group. Chemoimmunotherapy was associated with significantly higher rates of pathologic complete response (37.0% vs. 4.1%) and more pronounced nodal downstaging, with a higher proportion of patients achieving ypN0 status (76.1% vs. 34.0%). High tumoral PD-L1 expression (≥ 50%) and squamous cell carcinoma histology were independently associated with pathologic complete response. Real-world treatment with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy was feasible and resulted in improved response rates compared with chemotherapy, without increasing perioperative morbidity. Histology and high PD-L1 expression may serve as predictors for complete pathologic response, although the predictive value of PD-L1 requires confirmation in larger cohorts with more complete biomarker data.

RESULTS: Among patients with stage 1-3 NSCLC receiving lung resection (n = 59,226), 3% had cirrhosis with higher 30-day (5% versus 2%, p < 0.001) and 90-day (8% versus 3%, p < 0.001) mortality. After multivariable logistic regression, cirrhosis was associated with higher mortality odds at 30 days (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.39-3.99, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.38-3.21, p < 0.001); higher 90-day post-operative complications odds (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14-1.81, p = 0.002); and higher hospital readmission odds at 30 days (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.41-2.56, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.27-2.10, p = 0.001). Among those with stage 4 NSCLC (n = 27,357), adjusted Cox regression showed cirrhosis was associated with higher mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.016). However, when liver-related mortality was a competing event, association between cirrhosis and cancer-specific mortality was absent (sHR 1.04, 95% CI 0.95-1.13, p = 0.395). A lower proportion of patients with cirrhosis received systemic treatments (31% versus 40%, p < 0.001), and a greater proportion experienced post-treatment complications: electrolyte disturbances (10% versus 5%, p < 0.001), kidney injury (5% versus 2%, p = 0.012), and thrombocytopenia (7% versus 2%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhosis is associated with increased morbidity and mortality in stage 1-3 NSCLC patients undergoing curative surgery. Stage 4 NSCLC patients with cirrhosis are less likely to receive palliative treatment and may experience more post-treatment complications.

papers.abstract_en: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness and fatigability. Perioperative management is challenging because patients may have bulbar or respiratory muscle involvement and altered sensitivity to neuromuscular blocking agents, increasing the risk of postoperative respiratory failure and myasthenic crisis. Thymectomy is an established therapeutic option in selected patients with myasthenia gravis and may be performed using minimally invasive thoracoscopic techniques. We report the anesthetic management of a 48-year-old man with generalized acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MGFA class IIb) scheduled for thoracoscopic thymectomy. The patient had a recent relapse with diplopia, dysphagia, and easy fatigability, which improved after medical therapy. Preoperative optimization included intravenous immunoglobulin therapy for four days. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and remifentanil without initial neuromuscular blockade. Tracheal intubation was facilitated using video laryngoscopy after topical lidocaine. Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane, and invasive monitoring was established. Because of the surgical requirement for improved thoracoscopic visualization, a reduced dose of rocuronium was administered intraoperatively under train-of-four monitoring. At the end of surgery, neuromuscular blockade was reversed with sugammadex, and the patient was successfully extubated and transferred to the intensive care unit in stable condition. This case highlights the importance of careful preoperative optimization, avoidance of neuromuscular blocking agents when possible, quantitative neuromuscular monitoring, and individualized use of low-dose rocuronium with sugammadex reversal when muscle relaxation is required during thoracoscopic thymectomy in patients with myasthenia gravis.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: In the JCOG0802 study, segmentectomy demonstrated higher overall survival than did lobectomy, possibly due to a lower incidence of non-lung cancer death. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the cumulative incidence and factors associated with non-lung cancer death in patients with lung cancer who underwent curative resection. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, data from 1020 patients with stage 0-III lung cancer who underwent resection with lobectomy or segmentectomy between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Competing risk models (Fine and Gray) were used to estimate the cumulative incidence of non-lung cancer death and compare curves across clinicopathological factors. RESULTS: Among 1020 patients, 135 died from non-lung cancer causes. With lung cancer death treated as a competing event, the 10-year cumulative incidence of non-lung cancer death after resection was 18.6%. Multivariable analysis identified older age, comorbidity, low body mass index (BMI), and lobectomy as factors associated with a higher subdistribution hazard of non-lung cancer death. In an exploratory analysis of patients aged ≥ 71 years, older age, smoking history, low BMI, and lobectomy were associated with a higher cumulative incidence of non-lung cancer death in univariable analysis. No statistically significant interaction was observed between age and surgical procedure (P for interaction = 0.079). CONCLUSION: This study investigated the cumulative incidence of and risk factors for non-lung cancer death after lung cancer surgery. These findings suggest that patient characteristics should be considered when selecting the extent of lung resection.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The application of segmentectomy for deep-located tumors remains controversial as the result of margin concerns. This study evaluated septum-guided segmentectomy, which uses intersegmental septa and veins as anatomical boundaries to ensure precise dissection independent of fixed linear margin requirements. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 292 patients with deep-located cT1a-bN0M0 non-small cell lung cancer undergoing septum-guided segmentectomy (n = 130) or lobectomy (n = 162) via a minimally invasive approach (January 2019 to March 2025). To rigorously control for selection bias, propensity-score matching incorporating key physiological and anatomical confounders was performed, generating 88 well-balanced matched pairs (n = 176). Perioperative outcomes, locoregional recurrence, recurrence-free survival, and overall survival were evaluated. RESULTS: After propensity-score matching, baseline balance was achieved across key covariates. Survival analysis using stratified methods revealed no significant differences in recurrence-free survival or overall survival between the groups (P> .05). Notably, despite a substantial proportion of patients in the segmentectomy group not fulfilling standard National Comprehensive Cancer Network margin criteria (>20 mm or greater tumor size)-with a mean margin distance of 14.1 mm-no locoregional recurrence was observed during follow-up. R0 resection was achieved in all patients. Although segmentectomy involved longer operative times (P< .001), perioperative complications and hospital stays were highly comparable between the 2 cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Septum-guided segmentectomy demonstrates preliminary oncologic safety and perioperative outcomes comparable with lobectomy for deep-located early-stage non-small cell lung cancer. By using the intersegmental septum as a reliable anatomical barrier, this concept establishes a precise surgical paradigm that safely reduces the reliance on fixed margin distances.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) ranging from 30% to 50% have been recognized as a major threat to postoperative recovery. Current conventional interventions cannot effectively reduce the occurrence of PPCs. OBJECTIVE: In this study, we aimed to investigate the effects of multiple low-dose intranasal dexmedetomidine administration on PPCs in elderly patients. METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, elderly patients were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive multiple low-dose intranasal dexmedetomidine administration (MD group) or normal saline nasal spray (NS group). The primary outcome was the incidence of PPCs within 7 days after surgery. Key secondary outcomes included the severity grading and classification of PPCs. Other secondary outcomes included serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels, Richards-Campbell sleep questionnaire (RCSQ) scores at predefined time points, and adverse reactions. RESULTS: A total of 190 patients were screened, and 186 completed the study. The incidence of PPCs was significantly lower in the MD group than in the NS group (9.68% vs. 22.58%, P = 0.017), with a risk ratio (RR) of 2.333 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.173-6.317], absolute risk reduction (ARR) of 12.90%, and number needed to treat (NNT) of 7.75. Sensitivity analyses using the per-protocol population (PP) dataset yielded consistent results, confirming the stability and reliability of the primary outcome. The distribution of severity grading of PPCs also differed significantly between the groups (P = 0.036). After Bonferroni correction, the between-group difference in PPCs severity grading was not statistically significant (corrected P = 0.072). The distribution of pneumonia also differed significantly between the groups (P = 0.029). There were significant group effects, time effects, and interaction effects for IL-6, TNF-α, and RCSQ in the two groups after surgery (all P < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in drug-related adverse events. CONCLUSION: Multiple low-dose intranasal dexmedetomidine administration significantly reduces the incidence of PPCs in elderly patients undergoing radical thoracoscopic lung-cancer resection with a favorable safety profile. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary health care (PHC) offers a strategic opportunity to conduct research with immunotherapeutic products for cancer treatment. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the implementation of a program for conducting oncological clinical trials in PHC settings. The implementation objectives focused on assessing structure, process, and outcome indicators against predefined standards; the intervention objectives compared process and clinical outcomes (overall survival, quality of life, and patient satisfaction) in PHC settings against a historical control from secondary care. METHODS: A longitudinal, prospective, analytical implementation study was conducted in Cuba between January 2016 and August 2023. An open-label, uncontrolled, non-randomized, multicenter, phase IV clinical trial using the CIMAvax-EGF vaccine for patients with advanced lung cancer was used as a case study. The implementation was conducted in three phases: pilot study, replication, and generalization. This paper presents the outcomes of the generalization phase. For evaluation, structure, process, and outcome indicators were assessed against predefined standards and compared with a historical control from secondary health care (SHC). An indicator was considered adequate if it met the standard. The overall dimension (structure, process, or outcome) was considered acceptable if ≥ 70% of its indicators were adequate. RESULTS: The program was implemented in 119 polyclinics nationwide. For structure, 83% (5/6) of indicators were adequate; for process, 83% (5/6) were adequate; for outcome, 100% (4/4) were adequate. All three dimensions met the predefined standards. Process and outcome indicators were comparable or superior to the SHC historical control. Structure and outcome indicators improved after implementation. CONCLUSIONS: The results support the feasibility and effectiveness of implementing oncological clinical trials in Cuban PHC centers, demonstrating a positive impact on the target population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ciprofol is a novel intravenous anesthetic with potentially improved hemodynamic stability and fewer injection-related adverse effects than propofol. This study compared ciprofol and propofol for general anesthesia in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind trial, 120 adults undergoing elective thoracoscopic surgery were randomized to ciprofol (n = 60) or propofol (n = 60). MAP, HR, and BIS were assessed at eight predefined perioperative time points using linear mixed-effects models. The repeated binary outcome of BIS ≥60 was analyzed using a generalized linear mixed-effects model. Induction characteristics, injection pain, recovery profiles, and perioperative adverse events were also evaluated. RESULTS: MAP differed significantly between groups, with higher values in the ciprofol group at loss of consciousness and after tracheal intubation. HR was modestly higher at selected early time points, without a significant group-by-time interaction. BIS was higher with ciprofol during the early intraoperative period, and BIS ≥60 was more frequent at loss of consciousness (76.7% vs. 43.3%, p < 0.001), but not thereafter. Ciprofol was associated with shorter induction time (38.3 vs. 46.0 s, p < 0.001), less injection pain (5.0% vs. 20.0%, p = 0.025), and shorter PACU stay (48.0 vs. 55.7 min, p = 0.011). No significant differences were observed in supplemental anesthetic requirements, emergence time, or perioperative adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: Ciprofol showed a perioperative profile broadly comparable to propofol, with transient differences in hemodynamic parameters and higher BIS during the early intraoperative period. Ciprofol was associated with faster induction, less injection pain, and shorter PACU stay. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and resistance to targeted therapy and immunotherapy represents a substantial unmet clinical need. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic class. AREAS COVERED: This drug evaluation summarizes the pharmacological rationale, molecular design, preclinical activity, clinical efficacy, safety profile, and regulatory development of sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT; MK-2870/SKB264) in NSCLC. Relevant evidence was identified through searches of PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, major oncology congress proceedings, and regulatory announcements through 20 September 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Randomized trials have demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) with sac-TMT versus docetaxel and platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced NSCLC after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) progression. In advanced NSCLC without actionable driver alterations, sac-TMT plus pembrolizumab improved PFS versus pembrolizumab alone in programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-positive disease; however, overall survival (OS) remains immature, and superiority over contemporary chemoimmunotherapy has not been established. The principal clinically relevant toxicities are hematologic toxicity and stomatitis. Future studies should clarify predictive biomarkers, optimal treatment sequencing, intracranial activity, and generalizability, while generating mature survival and quality-of-life data.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assays can transform patient management by enabling molecular residual disease (MRD) detection, prognosis prediction, and treatment monitoring. Here, we report clinical performance of Signatera™ Genome, a whole genome sequencing (WGS)-based ctDNA assay, in a diverse pan-cancer cohort at landmark and longitudinal settings post-definitive treatment. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of 386 patients with one of the following cancers: breast, colorectal, non-small cell lung, melanoma, or renal cell carcinoma. Signatera™ Genome assays, designed with high-quality variants selected from the matched tumor and normal WGS data, were used to detect ctDNA in the associated patients' longitudinal plasma samples collected post-operatively. The correlation between ctDNA-based MRD status and systemic, distant recurrence-free survival (systemic DRFS) was assessed using Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: In the pan-cancer cohort, landmark analysis at 3 months post-surgery revealed that patients with MRD-positivity had significantly inferior systemic DRFS compared to ctDNA-negative patients (HR: 23.7, p < 0.0001). Additionally, ∼30% improvement in 24-month systemic DRFS was observed among adjuvant-treated MRD-positive patients, whereas MRD-negative patients derived no clear benefit from adjuvant therapy. In the longitudinal setting, MRD positivity anytime post-definitive treatment surveillance significantly correlated with shorter systemic DRFS compared to serial MRD negativity (HR: 104.7, p < 0.0001). Tumor-specific analyses yielded similar findings. Notably, 62% (72/116) of patients had ctDNA detected in the ultra-sensitive range of < 100 ppm. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings underscore the robust clinical performance of the Signatera Genome assay for MRD detection across solid tumors. Its broad applicability and high specificity support its integration into clinical practice and prospective trials.

papers.abstract_en: Objective: Treating lung cancer with a combination of targeted cancer therapy, supportive, and psychosocial treatments is important in modern oncology. The ACCEPT study investigated the efficacy of a 12-week early multimodal supportive care program on quality of life. Methods: ACCEPT was a single-center, non-randomized, prospective, open-label trial, with a pragmatic real-world design guided by patient choice. Patients with newly diagnosed, stage II-IV lung cancer participated in the outpatient ACCEPT program (psycho-oncology, health education, and training-based interventions alongside standard care). Longitudinal patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were collected. The primary outcome was the change in quality of life at 12 weeks measured by the Trial Outcome Index (TOI). Secondary outcomes included further exploratory PROM changes and overall survival. Results: Between April 2018 and August 2021, 214 lung cancer patients (median age 67, 53% male, 57% stage IV) were enrolled, with 116 patients evaluable for longitudinal PROM changes at 12 weeks. Participation in the multimodal ACCEPT program was associated with up to 17% improvement in the TOI, psychological distress, and sleep quality (p < 0.0001). Multivariate analyses revealed that greater session attendance was significantly and dose-dependently associated with improvements in the TOI as well as reductions in depression and anxiety. Higher engagement in multimodal sessions was also linked to reduced fatigue. Furthermore, exploratory signals of improved overall survival were observed among the 40 patients (18.7%) who fully completed the ACCEPT program. Conclusions: This pragmatic, patient-centered, multimodal supportive care program for lung cancer patients was associated with dose-dependent improvements in quality of life and psychological distress. While exploratory signals of improved survival were observed, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these findings and firmly establish the role of such supportive care programs in routine oncology.

papers.abstract_en: KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a clinically actionable molecular subtype. Discovery of the switch-II pocket enabled the development of covalent KRAS G12C(OFF)-state inhibitors, transforming a historically "undruggable" target into a therapeutic vulnerability. Drugging KRAS, however, proved to be a problem of chemistry, whereas sustaining its inhibition has proved to be a problem of biology. KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC is biologically heterogeneous, and the magnitude and durability of clinical benefit are shaped by co-mutations, the tumor microenvironment, brain metastases status, pharmacologic differences between agents, and the dynamic evolution of resistance. Randomized trials have demonstrated that sotorasib and adagrasib improve progression-free survival (PFS) and objective response rates (ORR) over docetaxel in previously treated disease, yet these gains have not translated consistently into a definitive overall survival (OS) advantage. This review synthesizes the epidemiology, molecular biology, diagnostic strategies, first- and later-line treatment evidence, resistance mechanisms, and emerging KRAS/RAS-directed approaches. We distinguish randomized or guideline-supported practice from early-phase and translational signals, and propose an implementable framework that combines PD-L1, tumor mutational burden, STK11/KEAP1/TP53 status, TTF-1 expression, brain metastases, and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for risk stratification and mechanism-guided management. At disease progression, oligoprogression should be distinguished from systemic progression, and tissue re-biopsy together with plasma profiling should be considered when feasible. In China, several domestically developed KRAS G12C inhibitors have been approved, and reimbursement coverage is expanding; the cost of molecular testing, uneven institutional access, regional disparities and limited confirmatory and real-world evidence nonetheless continue to constrain implementation. Future priorities include randomized first-line comparisons, biomarker-defined combination strategies, improved central nervous system activity and mechanism-matched treatment after resistance.

It is well known that traditional log-rank test no longer provides optimal power in this case. There has been a great interest to search for a more powerful test to detect a truly effective immunotherapy treatment. In this paper, we propose a new testing method based on the maximum value of a set of 0-1 weighted log-rank test statistics and establish useful theoretical results of the relevant test statistics. Extensive simulation studies are conducted to examine the empirical performance of the proposed method. An analysis of the real data from a non-small-cell lung cancer clinical trial is also carried out to further demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed test method. papers.abstract_en: The evaluation of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) is a persistent clinical challenge, made more pressing by the expansion of low-dose CT lung cancer screening. Conventional and earlier navigational bronchoscopy, including electromagnetic navigation, historically achieved diagnostic yields of approximately 60-70%, with CT-to-body divergence contributing to nondiagnostic sampling. This narrative review, prepared using the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA), summarizes robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) platform technology, procedural optimization, diagnostic performance, safety, molecular tissue adequacy, and emerging applications. A structured search was updated through September 2026; this is not a systematic review. Using the strict definition recommended by the American Thoracic Society/American College of Chest Physicians (ATS/ACCP), the most comprehensive meta-analysis reported a pooled RAB diagnostic yield of 69.6%, while the prospective multicenter TARGET study reported an adjudicated strict yield of 61.6%. Higher pooled estimates of approximately 84-87% generally use intermediate definitions that the ATS/ACCP statement recommends against as primary diagnostic-yield measures. RAB pneumothorax rates are approximately 2% in pooled analyses, compared with approximately 20-25% for CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy. In the randomized RELIANT trial, RAB was non-inferior, but not superior, to electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy; in VERITAS, navigational bronchoscopy as a category was non-inferior to transthoracic needle biopsy for 12-month diagnostic accuracy, with fewer pneumothoraces. RAB is a useful option for selected PPLs, but strict-definition performance is more modest than frequently quoted intermediate yields. Outcomes depend on lesion characteristics, sampling strategy, operator experience, center volume, and imaging infrastructure.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, accuracy, and safety of a novel extended reality-assisted percutaneous localization technique in a hybrid operating room for patients with small pulmonary nodules. METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm study, 20 adult patients scheduled for video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery sublobar resection for peripheral pulmonary nodules (2 cm or less) were enrolled. Participants underwent extended reality-guided percutaneous dye localization under general anesthesia. Patient-specific 3-dimensional holographic models were registered using optical markers to guide needle insertion, followed by confirmatory cone-beam computed tomography. The primary outcomes were technical accuracy and procedural safety. RESULTS: The extended reality-assisted technique achieved a 90% technical success rate. The mean localization error was 7.9 mm in the intention-to-treat population. The procedure was efficient, with a median localization time of 13.5 minutes and a median of 1 confirmatory cone-beam computed tomography scan. The complication rate was 5%, involving a single case of pneumothorax; no intrapulmonary hemorrhage or air embolism occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Extended reality-assisted percutaneous localization in a hybrid operating room is feasible and safe, demonstrating acceptable accuracy for small pulmonary nodules. This approach may streamline surgical workflow by enabling continuous needle advancement and reducing repetitive interruptions compared with conventional cone-beam computed tomography guidance.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is increasingly a disease of older age, and as low-dose computed tomography screening extends into the ninth decade, a growing number of octogenarians present with early-stage, potentially curable non-small cell lung cancer. Faced with these patients, clinicians repeatedly ask a single question: is this patient too old for surgery? Recent prospective data show that selected octogenarians achieve long-term survival comparable to younger patients despite substantially higher complication rates, with quality of life that recovers over the first postoperative year. Yet the favorable result is attributed to careful selection that is rarely defined, and is seldom accompanied by any account of the patients who were assessed and not offered an operation. This article argues that chronological age is the wrong axis for the decision. Physiologic reserve, measurable through validated frailty instruments and established physiologic testing, predicts postoperative outcome far better than birth year, and aging is sufficiently heterogeneous that any age threshold misclassifies patients in both directions. A substantial competing risk of non-cancer death, compounded by overdiagnosis among screen-detected tumors, tempers the survival gain expected from aggressive treatment and makes overtreatment as real a hazard as age-based exclusion. A graded menu of options now exists, extending from minimally invasive lobectomy through sublobar resection and stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to active surveillance, and intensity should descend with reserve rather than with age. The task is to operationalize careful selection through structured geriatric assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, prehabilitation, and shared decision-making, and to judge success by outcomes that older patients actually value.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in lung cancer may be coded as immune, marrow suppression, coagulation, or non-specific. We tested whether coding-defined report phenotypes differed across co-reported treatment contexts. METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2015Q1-2026Q2) and JADER through Japanese fiscal 2025Q4 (31 March 2026). Strict primary lung cancer reports were grouped as ICI without chemotherapy (C1), ICI plus chemotherapy (C2), or chemotherapy without ICI (C3). Firth models compared mutually exclusive immune-like and marrow-like anchors. Complementary analyses evaluated the broad cohort, treatment date compatibility, C3 small-cell influence, phenotype variants, onset windows, treatment-variable ablation in elastic-net report phenotype models, and a 120-report random stratified blinded review with independent ratings, third-person adjudication, inverse-selection weighting, and bootstrap uncertainty. RESULTS: FAERS included 1,362 immune-like or marrow-like anchors. Relative to C1, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for immune-like versus marrow-like phenotype were 0.111 (95% CI, 0.069-0.173) in C2 and 0.014 (0.006-0.029) in C3; C3 was exploratory because only eight reports were immune-like. In 2,835 broad cohort reports, adjusted immune-like composition was 13.0% (95% bootstrap interval, 11.0%-15.1%) in C1 and 4.7% (3.4%-6.2%) in C2. Treatment date and stricter phenotype analyses were directionally consistent. JADER reproduced the C2 versus C1 direction but showed calibration shift; treatment-variable ablation reduced cross-database discrimination. Reviewers agreed on 111/120 reports (92.5%; 95% CI, 87.5%-96.7%; Cohen's κ, 0.897; Gwet's AC1, 0.901). In the locked 927-report frame, design-weighted final categories were 23.4% immune probable, 37.3% immune possible, 13.6% indeterminate, and 25.8% non-immune probable. Among 100 determinate reports, weighted AUROC was 0.892 (0.827-0.948), PR-AUC 0.956 (0.922-0.982), and calibration-in-the-large intercept 2.054 (1.707-2.432), indicating underprediction. CONCLUSION: Coding-defined thrombocytopenia report composition differed across treatment contexts. Blinded review supported reproducible structured category assignment and score-based report ordering, while calibration shift and treatment-variable ablation defined important limits. Findings support pharmacovigilance case prioritization and hypothesis generation, not clinical diagnosis, incidence estimation, patient-level etiologic attribution, or causal inference.

papers.abstract_en: This paper presents a lung nodule detection and false positive reduction approach based on YOLOv8x, multi-view CT representations, and background slices used as negative samples. Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and early detection is essential to improve patient survival. Although computed tomography (CT) provides detailed three-dimensional information about the lungs, the large number of generated slices increases the complexity of radiological analysis and can contribute to diagnostic errors. To address this challenge, Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) systems have been developed to assist radiologists in identifying suspicious regions. In this work, we combine axial, coronal, and sagittal representations in a single YOLOv8x detection pipeline, use additional LIDC-IDRI annotation clusters with fewer than three radiologist markings as auxiliary positive samples, and introduce nodule-free background slices as negative training samples. Detections are consolidated through intra-view clustering and weighted inter-view fusion. Experiments following the LUNA16 cross-validation protocol show that the proposed strategy improves detection performance while substantially reducing false positives. The axial baseline achieved a Competition Performance Metric (CPM) score of 0.553 with 32.61 candidates per scan, whereas the multi-view configuration with a nominal budget of 20,000 background images achieved a CPM score of 0.863 and reduced the average number of candidates to 9.11 per scan while preserving high sensitivity. These results show that the combined use of multiple anatomical views and background-negative training can substantially reduce spurious candidates in CT-based lung nodule detection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer mortality, and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is largely driven by the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), in which tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are major regulators. OBJECTIVES: This review summarizes recent advances in understanding TAM heterogeneity, their contribution to immune resistance in NSCLC, and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TAMs. METHODS: A literature search was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar, focusing on studies published between 2021 and 2025. Key search terms included "non-small cell lung cancer", "tumor immune microenvironment", "macrophage heterogeneity", "M1 macrophages", "M2 macrophages", "SPP1+ macrophages", "TREM2+ macrophages", "immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance", "macrophage metabolic reprogramming", and "TAM-targeted therapies". Relevant studies addressing TAM heterogeneity, immune resistance, metabolic and molecular regulation, and therapeutic targeting in NSCLC were prioritized, while earlier studies were included where necessary to provide mechanistic context. RESULTS: Recent evidence demonstrates that TAMs comprise diverse functional subsets rather than a simple M1/M2 duality. Distinct populations including CXCL9+, SPP1+, C1Q+, and TREM2+ macrophages differentially regulate T-cell exclusion, immune checkpoint resistance, angiogenesis, and metabolic remodeling. Therapeutic approaches targeting CSF1R, CD47-SIRPα, metabolic pathways, nanoparticles, epigenetic regulators, engineered macrophages, and microRNA-based strategies show promise but remain limited by macrophage plasticity and compensatory immune mechanisms. CONCLUSION: A comprehensive understanding of TAM heterogeneity within the tumor immune microenvironment provides a framework for overcoming immune resistance in NSCLC. Future therapeutic strategies should integrate biomarker-guided patient selection with combination approaches that simultaneously target macrophage plasticity and immune suppression.

papers.abstract_en: Newborn screening (NBS) based on T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) has revolutionized the early diagnosis of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), facilitating the identification of affected newborns before the onset of life-threatening infections. However, reduced TRECs levels are a surrogate marker of impaired thymic output rather than a disease-specific finding. Accordingly, low values can result from highly heterogeneous and distinct biological mechanisms of T-cell ontogeny that extend beyond classical SCID phenotypes. This study describes three patients with inborn errors of immunity (IEI) identified through abnormal TRECs screening who were subsequently diagnosed with Artemis, FOXN1, and Moesin deficiencies. These clinical cases demonstrate that primary T-cell immunodeficiencies can arise from defects at distinct biological levels of T-cell development, specifically in impaired antigen receptor V(D)J recombination (characteristic of NHEJ deficiencies and other SCID conditions), disrupted thymic stromal microenvironment function and compromised peripheral lymphocyte homeostasis, respectively. Consequently, optimizing clinical outcomes after a positive newborn screening requires the systematic integration of clinical, immunological and molecular findings. This diagnostic approach should involve specialized immunodeficiency centers with access to advanced flow cytometry techniques and molecular confirmation to ensure an accurate and definitive diagnosis. Ultimately, therapeutic decisions from supportive care to definitive hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or gene/enzymatic therapy for SCID patients must be guided by the precise underlying pathogenic mechanism and the specific molecular defect.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Persistent lung cancer mortality despite screening is multifactorial. Characterizing computed tomography (CT) findings preceding fatal lung cancer may identify imaging features and screening challenges that warrant further study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, outcome-enriched case series nested within the 26,722-participant low-dose computed tomography arm of the National Lung Screening Trial. Among 359 participants who died of lung cancer within the prespecified interval, exclusions for positive baseline screening (n = 186), incomplete screening (n = 28), withdrawal/declined screening (n = 19), unavailable CTs (n = 6), or three negative screens followed by death 2+ years after the final screen (n = 29) yielded 91 participants. Screening CTs were retrospectively assessed using the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) v2022. Four thoracic radiologists independently reviewed visible-in-retrospect nodules and adjudicated whether they met criteria for suspicion. RESULTS: Of 91 participants, 22 (24%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 17%-34%) had visible-in-retrospect nodules considered suspicious under Lung-RADS v2022 ("missed"), 16 (18%; 95% CI, 11%-27%) had visible nodules not meeting suspicion criteria ("not callable"), 50 (55%; 95% CI, 45%-65%) had no visible-in-retrospect nodule, and 3 (3.3%) were inconclusive. Missed nodules were frequently juxtapleural (41%), obscured (50%), or irregularly bordered (68%); not-callable nodules were frequently <6 mm (75%), juxtapleural (56%), or irregularly bordered (56%). CONCLUSION: In this selected fatal-case series, small and juxtapleural nodules were common among visible nodules not meeting Lung-RADS v2022 suspicion criteria. These findings warrant evaluation in representative screening populations and should not be interpreted as estimates of population-level Lung-RADS performance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: We evaluated 10 years of QOPI implementation in Spain to characterize quality performance across successive stages of participation, assess sustainability over time, compare performance with contemporaneous QOPI benchmarks, identify persistent certification gaps, and examine quality performance across repeated certification and reassessment cycles. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We conducted a longitudinal descriptive study of QOPI implementation in Spanish oncology practices between 2015 and 2025. Analyses included within-practice changes in QOPI quality measures among certified practices, comparing the last available pre-certification assessment with the first post-certification assessment, including disease-specific measures for breast, colorectal, and lung cancer; descriptive comparisons between first participation and post-certification assessments, benchmarking against the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate, and findings from external certification and recertification surveys. RESULTS: Within-practice longitudinal analyses among certified practices showed higher post-certification performance in several patient-centered measures, including emotional well-being assessment (75.56% to 85.20%), infertility risk discussion (70.33% to 78.67%), appropriate pain management (83.57% to 89.15%), and pain assessment (83.56% to 89.50%). Certified practices maintained broadly high performance over time, although lower post-certification performance was observed in some chemotherapy and other documentation measures. Benchmarking showed a shift: pain assessment, emotional well-being assessment, appropriate pain management, and infertility counseling moved from below to above the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate after certification. External surveys identified recurrent opportunities for improvement in treatment verification and patient information and education. CONCLUSION: A decade of QOPI implementation in Spain was associated with sustained high-quality performance, higher scores in selected patient-centered measures after certification, and the identification of persistent opportunities for improvement. Repeated measurement, benchmarking, certification, and reassessment may support organizational change and continuous quality improvement.
